# nUIget 2.0 — item tracker

One row per work item of `2026-10-11-nuiget-2.0-execution-plan.md`, in execution order. `RUN.md` reads this file to pick
the next item and updates the row when the item closes. Status values: `open`, `in-progress`, `done`, `blocked`, `skipped`
(owner decision). The `commit` column holds the SHA on `labs/2.0` that closed the item; findings are tracked in
`findings-ledger.md`.

Rows P5.1, P5.3 and P5.4 run before P4 by the P3.6 ruling; the phase review of P4 (`git log labs/2.0-P3-done..HEAD`)
therefore covers them, and the P5 review covers `labs/2.0-P4-done..HEAD`. The phase gates and tags are unchanged.

```text
VERDICT: PASS

Correction to the brief first (agent rule: say when the brief is wrong about the tree). The frozen-path statement "changed only in P0.0 (004-sdk-probes.md), P0.1 and P0.9" is incomplete: commit 1d26aeb (P0.0) also edited `/Users/mattias/github/nuiget/docs/adr/README.md` (lines 19-22, a "Supplements" list linking `004-sdk-probes.md`). The edit is index-only, changes no decision text, pre-dates the hook (P0.5), and is recorded as a deviation in `/Users/mattias/github/nuiget/src/core/cli/STATUS.md:47`. It is not a defect; it belongs in the record. `git log origin/main..HEAD -- docs/adr src/protocol src/core/contracts.ts` lists exactly 1d26aeb and 583ef41; `src/protocol/**` and `src/core/contracts.ts` do not exist on the branch.

NON-BLOCKING:
1. Local gate for 2.0 items does not type-check their tests. Plan §2.2 step 5 runs `npx tsc --noEmit` (main program, `tsconfig.json`, which excludes `src/**/*.test.ts`); `tsc -p tsconfig.vitest.json` runs only inside `npm run check-types`, which the step list reaches only through `npm run package:vsix` (host/service/esbuild items). CI's Build & Package job runs `npm run check-types` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, "Type check" step), so a core item with type errors in its tests is caught only after the push.    Answers to question 2. Blocking: yes, before P3.3 (its row already says so). The generation travels as a field, not a wrapped return: `RequestContext<T>` (`WebviewHost.ts:35-40`) gains `generation?: number`, documented "set by a handler whose result is a coordinator resource: the generation it was computed for; `WebviewHost` puts it on the ok envelope (ADR-007)"; `dispatch` posts `makeOk(request.id, request.type, result, ctx.generation)`; an error response, a stream chunk and an aborted request never carry it. The `RequestHandler` type and the 43 one-response cases are untouched by this choice.

   Catalog (`src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts`): `export interface CatalogValue<T> { value: T; generation: number }`; `projects`, `sources` and `transitive` return `Promise<CatalogValue<…>>` with `generation: handle.generation` of the handle whose `value` resolved (`queryWithRetry` returns `{ value, generation }` of the attempt that succeeded, so a stale retry reports the new generation); `InstalledQueryResult` gains `generation: number`, the handle's generation of the attempt that resolved, the same for the `{ result }` of a cache hit or joiner, for the `{ result, upgrade }` of a running evaluation, and for the provisional that `upgrade` falls back to when the evaluation is superseded (that fallback is then below the generation the event lists, which is exactly what the webview must discard; note on the P6.2 row that this fallback, `Catalog.ts:132`, becomes the first real producer of such a response). A cache hit reports `entry.generation` (equal to `valueGeneration` by the hit condition, `QueryCoordinator.ts:158-160`); a joiner reports the computation's generation; both surfaces therefore see the same number for the same `(key, generation)`. The fan-outs `allProjectsInstalled` and `allProjectsTransitive` unwrap `.value` internally (`Catalog.ts:205,214,246,253`) and report no generation: they are not resources (ADR-009 decision 1).

Follow-up ruling on P7.fix-4 (the DetailsPane test not named by the review), verbatim:

`````text
Follow-up ruling on PHASE REVIEW P7, P7.fix-4 (DO 2-3), the DetailsPane test not named by the review.

DECISION: Option 2. Drop the `all.status !== 'ready'` term from the Install button (my DO 2 over-specified it); keep `listed()`, `blocked` and the two notes; `src/webview/main/features/details/DetailsPane.test.tsx` `a browse selection under All Projects opens the project picker and installs into the projects picked` stays byte for byte; the new late-chunk title loses "and the Install button waits" and gains a `checking` assertion for the late chunk.

WHY: The invariant that matters is "every project in `onInstall`'s list has a `result` and, if CPM, a `null` preview", and it holds without the status term. A project without a chunk is `blocked` by `listed()`; a listed CPM project is in `cpmKey`, so the `[bus, cpmKey, packageId, version]` effect of `MultiInstallDialog.tsx` previews it with `checking` true and filters `picked` afterwards; a chunk that arrives later (a new project, or a provisional → authoritative upgrade that changes `isCpm`) changes `cpmKey`, re-arms `checking` and re-filters. The status term therefore only made Install wait for projects nobody picked, on a large workspace the whole fan-out. The failing test (`DetailsPane.test.tsx:299-326`) models exactly that real stream (chunks shown, answer pending) and its expectation is the right behaviour, so the code bends, not the test; plan §3 prefers the option that keeps tests intact, and no test the review named changes either.

```text
DECISION: Option 1. Every OPEN point is ruled below; nothing in the row is the owner's. Rulings on the open points: 3 = `ProjectMutator` with the two query members P6.3 names (`canMutate`, `previewCpmImpact`) over named request/decision types, no `apply`; 4 = `resourceKeys.sources(projectDir)` with a required argument; 5 = literal request name `'readme/image'` placed in the Package details group, payload `{ url: string; sourceUrl?: string }`, result `{ url: string; dataUri: string | null }`; 7 = `generation?: number` on the ok variant of `ResponseEnvelope` only (not on result types, not on `StreamEnvelope`), with an optional fourth parameter on `makeOk`; 8 = the naming rule is recorded in ADR-007 and its consequences are exactly: the three `source?: string` payload fields → `sourceUrl?`, the two `resourceKeys` parameters → `sourceUrl`, `search/query.sources?: string[]` → `sourceUrls?`; `selectedSource`, `search/autocomplete.sources`, `removedUrl`, `disabledUrl`, `NuGetSource.url`, `FailedSource.url` keep their names; 9 = export the union as `CapabilityProvenance`; 11 = no contract edit in P1.1b, the P1.6 row carries `AddPackageOptions.isCpm`; ADR-005 = strike `undici`, make the proxy sentence equal to the `Transport` comment at `src/core/contracts.ts:238-242`, name `ProjectExecutionContext` as the context contract, leave the configuration matrix and the vendoring decision to P4.1; amendments are written inline in the form ADR-000 used in P0.9, not as appended sections; the N42 order (tracker, sentinel, protocol note) is right.

WHY: I verified every path:line in the brief against `labs/2.0` @ ac64e72 and all hold: `src/core/contracts.ts:98` has `rejected: (reason: string) => T`, `:173-174` says "merged over the sanitized base env", `:185-192` still declares `nounFirstSyntax`, `:307-314` declares `CpmImpactPreview`; `src/protocol/domain.ts:69` lacks `sdk-too-old` and `:225` is `sources: (): ResourceKey => 'sources'`; `src/protocol/messages.ts:131` lacks `sourcesUnavailable` while `:121` and `:127` already carry it as optional; `src/protocol/envelope.ts:48-50` is the two-variant union; ADR-005 says "via `https.Agent`/`undici` proxy agent" and ADR-006 says "`readme/image` lazily". Three facts the brief did not carry decide the open points: (i) ADR-000's amendment of P0.9 (commit 583ef41) is inline, a header line `Status: accepted · Date: 2026-10-10 · Amended: 2026-10-12 (plan item P0.9: …)`, a Context paragraph and rewritten bullets, so appended sections would give the ADR set two forms and force readers to compute the effective decision from two texts; (ii) `tseslint.configs.recommended` is on (`eslint.config.mjs:92`) and includes `no-empty-object-type`, so option (c) for the mutator (an empty interface) is lint-red, and P6.3's row names core/project and host but not `contracts.ts`, so deferring members guarantees an unplanned contract-change item later; (iii) `domain.ts:260` already has `OperationKind = 'install' | 'update' | 'remove' | 'restore'` and the house shape for a failed result is `{ ok: false; error }` (`contracts.ts:257` `SourceMutationResult`, `domain.ts:272` `StepOutcome`, P1.10's refusal `{ ok:false, error:'…' }`), so the mutator reuses both instead of inventing `add` and `reason`. For 4, ADR-005 resolves sources per project directory and `SourceProvider.listSources(projectDir)` (`contracts.ts:264`) is per directory, so a bare `'sources'` key has no meaning and an optional argument would create two keys for one resource. For 5, the name `readme/image` appears in ADR-006 and in three plan rows (P1.1b, P4.4, P5.7) that are executed literally and that P7.5's drift script may grep; results echoing a request field is the house pattern (`package/versions` echoes `packageId`, `updates/get` echoes `projectPath`, `search/query` echoes `query`); `sourceUrl?` lets the host confine credentials to the README's own feed (ADR-006 "same host-side fetch … auth"), and a `null` data URI is ADR-006's "shown as links when the fetch fails". For 7, ADR-002 says "Request ids correlate RPC; generations establish freshness", which is a transport-level property, one declaration on the envelope serves every resource request without enumerating which results are resources, the guard `isResponseEnvelope` needs no change for an optional field, and streams need no generation because ADR-002 invariant 2 terminates a request whose generation is superseded with `StaleQueryError`, so a chunk never outlives its generation and chunks are dropped by request id alone. For 8, ADR-007's Context already names "the same concept had different field names per surface" as the problem it solves, so that is where the rule belongs; `ProjectExecutionContext.sourceUrls` (`contracts.ts:290`) and `BulkPackageRef.sourceUrl` (`messages.ts:42`) are the precedent. For 11, `AddPackageOptions` is an argv-builder option type internal to `src/core/cli`, not a cross-module contract, and moving it would make P1.6's copy of `commands.ts` collide with a declaration in `contracts.ts`, forcing a delete-and-reimport; that loses work if P1.6 is interrupted. For ADR-005, the P4.1 row (plan line 257) owns "supported configuration and matrix; decide on vendoring a proxy agent" and D6 lists P4.1 as the ADR-005 contract item, so P1.1b writes only what is already decided and already stated in `contracts.ts:238-242`.

DECISION: (1) Option 1a, confined to `src/core/contracts.ts`: `InvalidationEvent.keys` becomes `Array<{ key: ResourceKey; generation: number }>`, the event's `generation` stays and is documented as a per-event sequence number that is not comparable with a key's generation; the per-key value is recorded at bump time (last bump in a coalesced tick wins, which equals the flush-time value). The protocol event `resources/invalidated`, ADR-002 and ADR-008 are not touched in P1.8; the protocol side goes to the item that first emits the event (P2.9/P2.10) under its own approval, with tracker notes written now. (2) A `carried: Set<Subscription>` on `Computation` — 2b's data structure with 2a's lifetime: a stale computation's unreleased `active` handles are moved into `next.carried` as a provisional keep-alive that ends when a consumer joins `next`, when `next` settles, at the next invalidation (carried handles never count for a further carry-over) or on an explicit `release()`, whichever comes first; liveness everywhere is `active.size + carried.size`. No ADR edit is needed for it. (3) The seven titles are literal `it()` titles, exactly as written in the row; extra tests are allowed and two are named below. The quarry working tree (with its uncommitted edits) is the base for the copy; "apply uncommitted refactor" and D3 mean the same thing.

WHY: D6 (plan line 50) and the recorded P1.1b rulings (`docs/plans/STATUS.md:33`, `:293`, `:310`, `:366`; `src/core/session/STATUS.md:136`) approve one thing for P1.8: the `InvalidationEvent` member of `src/core/contracts.ts`. The P1.8 row (plan line 215) names `InvalidationEvent.keys` and no protocol or ADR file, its gate is "tests green; eslint 0; tsc 0" with no `docs:protocol:check`, nothing in the tree consumes the event yet (grep above), and the advisor's own tiebreak is the narrowest contract and the least work lost: the first emitter (P2.9 `WebviewHost`, P2.10 "watcher → `resources/invalidated`", plan lines 233-234) and the first consumer (P3.3, line 246) settle the protocol shape with `docs:protocol:check` as their gate. Neither ADR describes the core member, so the contracts edit creates no ADR mismatch; the existing mismatch (ADR-002:56 broadcasts one global `generation`, ADR-008:21 compares per key) predates P1.8 and travels as tracker notes. 1a keeps `generation` because removing it would also change the protocol event and ADR-002:56; 1c leaves `keys` as it is, which is not what the row says ("`keys` carries"). For (2) the brief's reading of the leak is the right one: a carried subscription is already rejected, is never in `next.attached`, and in the quarry stays in `next.active` until the consumer releases a handle that already failed, so a consumer that re-queries without releasing (a) blocks the abort of `next` when its new handle is released, (b) is carried again on every later invalidation and starts a recompute for nobody, and (c) is held for the entry's lifetime. The carried set bounds that interest to one generation and to the first of four definite events, which keeps ADR-002 invariant 2 literally true ("recomputes if any subscriber remains": the carry test stays `current.active.size > 0`) and invariant 4 intact (joining replaces the provisional keep-alives, so "the last subscriber leaves" means the real ones). 2c would delete behaviour ADR-002 and the class comment describe for no gain in safety.

5. The `carryOver` fix. Types:
```ts
interface Subscription {
    released: boolean;
    deferred: Deferred;
    onChunk?: ChunkListener;
    /** Computation this subscription currently keeps alive (re-pointed when carried over). */
    owner: Computation;
}

interface Computation {
    key: ResourceKey;
    generation: number;
    controller: AbortController;
    compute: ComputeFn;
    /** Handles created for this computation; they receive its value and chunks. */
    attached: Set<Subscription>;
    /** Unreleased handles among `attached`. */
    active: Set<Subscription>;
    /**
     * Unreleased handles of the stale predecessor, already rejected with `StaleQueryError`. They keep this
     * recompute alive only until a consumer joins it, it settles or the next invalidation, and are never
     * carried a second time; they do not receive its value.
     */
    carried: Set<Subscription>;
    settled: boolean;
}
```
(keep the quarry's names for `Deferred`, `ChunkListener`, `ComputeFn`). `create()` initialises `carried: new Set()`. Two module-level helpers:
```ts
function isAlive(computation: Computation): boolean {
    return computation.active.size > 0 || computation.carried.size > 0;
}

/** End the provisional keep-alive of carried-over handles; a later `release()` of such a handle is a no-op. */
function dropCarried(computation: Computation): void {
    for (const subscription of computation.carried) {
        subscription.released = true;
    }
    computation.carried.clear();
}
```
`invalidate()`, per matching entry (the carry test stays `current.active.size > 0`; carried handles never count):
```ts
entry.generation++;
affected.set(key, entry.generation);
const current = entry.current;
if (!current) {
    continue;
}
entry.current = undefined;
current.controller.abort();
const stale = new StaleQueryError(key, current.generation);
for (const subscription of current.attached) {
    subscription.deferred.reject(stale);
}
if (!current.settled && current.active.size > 0) {
    this.carryOver(entry, current);
}
dropCarried(current);
```
`carryOver`:
```ts
/**
 * Start the recompute for the new generation right away and let the stale computation's unreleased handles
 * keep it alive provisionally, so a consumer that re-`query()`s on `StaleQueryError` joins work already in
 * flight. Only `active` handles are carried; a recompute kept alive solely by carried handles is not carried
 * again (see `invalidate`). The `compute` call is deferred by one microtask so a synchronous burst of
 * invalidations starts at most one recompute.
 */
private carryOver(entry: Entry, stale: Computation): void {
    const next = this.create(entry, stale.key, stale.compute);
    for (const subscription of stale.active) {
        subscription.owner = next;
        next.carried.add(subscription);
    }
    stale.active.clear();
    queueMicrotask(() => this.run(entry, next));
}

```ts
private release(entry: Entry, subscription: Subscription): void {
    if (subscription.released) {
        return;
    }
    subscription.released = true;
    const owner = subscription.owner;
    owner.active.delete(subscription);
    owner.carried.delete(subscription);
    if (isAlive(owner)) {
        return;
    }
    queueMicrotask(() => {
        if (isAlive(owner) || this.disposed) {
            return;
        }
        owner.controller.abort();
        if (!owner.settled && entry.current === owner) {
            entry.current = undefined;
        }
    });
}
```

```text
# ADR-009: Catalog, the use-case layer over the query coordinator

Status: accepted · Date: 2026-10-12

## Context

Two surfaces ask the same questions about the same projects, and in 1.x each panel composed the services itself (`NuGetPanel.ts`, `NuGetSidebarPanel.ts`): both computed updates for the same project with their own refresh verbs and caches. ADR-002 gives one computation per resource and generation; ADR-004 and ADR-005 give the project model and its execution context. Missing was the one place where a read request becomes a coordinator query over those modules, so that handlers stay thin and never compose core modules themselves. The quarry's `Catalog.ts` had that role but blocked on the evaluator, fabricated the execution context and took directories from `process.cwd()` (findings C-project-catalog-2, -3 and -6).

## Decision

1. Hosts read through the `Catalog` (`src/core/catalog`) and nowhere else. The Catalog has one method per read request of `RequestMap` (`src/protocol/messages.ts`) plus the two lookups `PackageWorkflows` needs (`packageDependencies`, `projectDependencies`). Every cacheable read is exactly one `QueryCoordinator.query` under the key that `resourceKeys` builds for that request, so both surfaces share one computation per generation. Reads that ADR-002 leaves without a key (`search/query`, `search/autocomplete`, `package/readme`, `transitive/metadata`) run directly. The `allProjects/*` methods are fan-outs over the per-project resources and are not coordinator resources themselves: a cache hit delivers the final value and no chunk, and the payload of an all-projects read is its chunks; the `allProjects:*` keys of `resourceKeys` stay reserved.
2. Streams are `emit` callbacks. The chunk types of the all-projects methods are the protocol's `RequestChunk<…>` types (type-only import), so the host forwards them unchanged. The coordinator caches what the compute function returns; a cache hit and a late joiner receive that value and no chunk, so the returned value is complete on its own and chunks only precede it.
3. `installed(projectPath)` resolves as soon as the provisional result exists, with `{ result, upgrade? }`. `upgrade` is present only when an evaluation has started; it resolves with the authoritative result, or with the provisional again when the evaluation fails or the generation is superseded, and it never rejects. The coordinator caches the authoritative result when there is one, so a cache hit and a joiner during the evaluation receive `{ result: authoritative }` without `upgrade`. The host streams the provisional as a chunk and sends the authoritative as the terminal response (ADR-007: chunks precede the response); the chunk kind that carries it is added to `installed/get` by the item that adds the evaluator (P6.2), which also decides when an evaluation is needed. An evaluation never runs for an `unsupported` project.
4. Every project-scoped read builds its `ProjectExecutionContext` through `ProjectContextProvider` (ADR-005), and nothing in `src/core/catalog` reads `process.cwd()`; a read that needs a directory without a project takes it from the caller (`sources(projectDir)`), and the host decides which directory that is. A context whose SDK is below 10 is reported as `InstalledResult.unsupported = { reason: 'sdk-too-old', message: 'requires .NET SDK 10 or newer' }` on the provisional result with its packages kept, because the project stays readable (D13); an `unsupported` set by the inspector is kept as it is. When the context cannot be built, the provisional result stands without evaluation and the failure is logged: a source listing that fails does not hide the package list.
5. Sources, outbound policy and credentials belong to a project context (ADR-005). A Catalog method resolves them from the context of the project the read is for, never from a workspace-wide default; the feed-dependent methods that consume them arrive with P4.9.
6. `invalidate(scope, reason)` is the single entry for invalidation. It always forwards to `QueryCoordinator.invalidate`; for the scopes `sources` and `workspace` it first clears the per-directory source listings (`SourceProvider.invalidate`), and P4.9 adds the service-index caches and `IconResolver.reset()` at the same place. Caches that check their inputs themselves (the mtime-keyed `AssetsReader`) are not cleared here.
7. A query handle is released when the caller's `AbortSignal` aborts; a call without a signal releases its handle when the value settles. A handle that rejects with `StaleQueryError` is released and the query is asked again, at most three times; the third `StaleQueryError` is thrown.
8. Breadth is frozen until P4 (plan §7): no use case is added to the Catalog without amending this record. The feed-dependent methods (`updates`, `allProjectsUpdates`, `transitiveMetadata`, `search`, `quickSearch`, `versions`, `metadata`, `readme`) are declared with domain-typed signatures and throw `NotYetAvailableError` (`code: 'not-yet-available'`) before creating any query handle until P4.9 wires the feeds; the host maps that error to the protocol error code `unsupported`.

## Consequences

- Handlers are thin: validate the payload, call one Catalog method, forward chunks, send one terminal response.
- Mutations never go through the Catalog: they are `PackageWorkflows` on the `OperationQueue` (ADR-003). The Catalog learns of them through `invalidate`.
- `search/query` carries `sourcesUnavailable` from the Catalog's `search` result (an unreachable source is not an empty result).

Composition in order: `output` + `logger` (step 4); `runner = new DefaultDotnetRunner({ logger, ...overrides })` (step 12) + hydrate + legacy sweep; `cache`; `sources = new DotnetSourceProvider({ runner, logger })`; `assets = new AssetsReader()`; `stopDirs`; `inspector`; `contexts = new ProjectContextProvider(...)`; `coordinator = new DefaultQueryCoordinator({ logger })`; `session = new DefaultSessionStore(context.workspaceState, logger)`; `queue = new DefaultOperationQueue({ maxWaiting: 5, logger })`; `catalog = new Catalog({ coordinator, inspector, contexts, sources, assets, discoverProjects, logger })` with `discoverProjects: () => findProjects(async (include, exclude, max) => (await vscode.workspace.findFiles(include, exclude, max)).map(u => u.fsPath), (vscode.workspace.workspaceFolders ?? []).map(f => ({ name: f.name, fsPath: f.uri.fsPath })))` (the `await` turns the Thenable into a Promise; no `Thenable` token); `workflows = new PackageWorkflows(createWorkflowDeps({ runner, catalog, inspector, queue, logger, onCommand }))` with the quarry's `onCommand` body writing through `logger`; `events = new HostEvents()`; `services: HostServices = { context, logger, session, catalog, queue, workflows, sources, onOperationCompleted: events.operationCompleted.event, onOperationProgress: queue.onProgress, onConfigChanged: events.configChanged.event, onProjectsChanged: events.projectsChanged.event, invalidate: (scope, reason) => catalog.invalidate(scope, reason), announceOperation: outcome => events.operationCompleted.fire(outcome), config: readExtensionConfig, workspaceFolderFor }` (no `vscode.Disposable.from` around core events). Subscriptions: `output`, `events`, `queue`, `coordinator`, `session` (`DefaultSessionStore.dispose` exists), `sidebar`, `registerWebviewViewProvider(SidebarHost.viewType, sidebar, { webviewOptions: { retainContextWhenHidden: true } })`, `{ dispose: () => MainPanelHost.instance?.dispose() }`, the status bar item, every watcher and timer.

(f) One `refreshProjectsAndSession()` with coalescing: a module-local `inFlight: Promise<void> | undefined` and `rerun = false`; a request while one runs sets `rerun = true`; when the run settles and `rerun` is set, it clears the flag and runs once more. Body: `lastReconciledProject = session.snapshot.selectedProject` first (so the host-origin commit that `reconcile` fires cannot re-trigger); `const projects = await catalog.projects()`; `events.projectsChanged.fire(projects)`; `await vscode.commands.executeCommand('setContext', 'nuiget.hasProjectFiles', projects.length > 0)`; `const directory = sourceDirectory(services)` (import from `./host/handlers`; wrap in try) and `const sources = await catalog.sources(directory)`; on success remember `lastListing = { directory, urls }` and `await session.reconcile(projects, enabledUrls)`. On a failed listing or a `not-found` from `sourceDirectory`: never pass `[]`; use `lastListing.urls` if `lastListing.directory === directory`, else `session.snapshot.selectedSource === 'all' ? [] : [session.snapshot.selectedSource]` (keeps the selection without claiming knowledge), log a warning, still call `reconcile` with the real `projects` (a deleted project must not stay selected). Triggers: at the end of `activateWith` (not awaited); from `coordinator.onDidInvalidate` when `event.scope.kind` is `workspace`, `project` or `sources` (not `package`, not `metadata`: they reach neither `projects` nor `sources:*`, `scopes.ts:15-17`); from `session.onDidChange` when `snapshot.selectedProject !== lastReconciledProject`. `afterSourceMutation` (`handlers.ts:307-312`) reconciles too; the duplicate is coalesced and idempotent. The intermediate broadcast between `apply` and `reconcile` stays acceptable; P2.11 proves convergence (P1.7 ruling).

### P2.11 — stop-and-ask: composition and scenarios of the two-surface harness (2026-10-13)

Brief: plan §2.4 form, item P2.11, on `labs/2.0` @ `3d1da7b` with nothing written. Two triggers: the row's
gate runs nothing until the `integration` project of `vitest.config.mts` includes the harness, and
`tsconfig.vitest.json`, which the row does not name, has to include it for the harness to be type-checked. The
brief also reported that no ok response carries a `generation` (`src/host/WebviewHost.ts:146`), and asked how
the harness is composed, what its fake webview models, which timers it fakes and what each of the seven
scenarios asserts. Answer, verbatim; no sentinel was created, because no frozen path changes:

`````text
DECISION: Composition A1 (the real root through `activateWith`, the real `SidebarHost` and `MainPanelHost` over the harness's own fake webviews; no hand-built `HostServices`, no `TestHost` subclass; the only injected seam is `vi.spyOn(services.workflows, 'single')` for the thrown exception), fake webview B2 (a recorder plus a seven-rule client model that `expectState` reads and that P3.3 later implements for real), timers D1 (fake `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` for the whole file, explicit `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` after a watcher fires, `vi.waitFor` everywhere else), and C1 sharpened for the missing response generation (finding C-protocol-host-7, fixed by a `P2.fix` item at the P2 phase review before P3.3; no P2.11 scenario depends on it). Config: `vitest.config.mts` integration include gains `src/test/harness/**/*.test.ts`; `tsconfig.vitest.json` include gains `src/test/harness/**/*.ts`, approved here as a file the row does not name; nothing in `eslint.config.mjs`, CI or `package.json`. Scenario `A→B→A ordering` proves the P1.7 condition (both surfaces converge) and drives the race deterministically; the selection it loses in that race is a root defect (C-state-core-6) that P2.11 records and does not fix: the fix is `P2.fix-1` at the phase review, with the harness as its oracle. Not `OWNER MUST DECIDE`.

WHY: The brief is right about the tree: `vitest.config.mts:86` includes only `src/test/integration/**/*.integration.test.ts`, so the row's gate would run nothing; `tsconfig.json:30-40` excludes `src/test` and `tsconfig.vitest.json:35-52` does not list a harness directory, so nothing would type-check it (N39, gotcha "Tests pass is not compiles"); `src/host/WebviewHost.ts:146` posts `makeOk(request.id, request.type, result)` and `src/protocol/envelope.ts:88-91` takes the optional fourth argument nobody passes, while ADR-007:29-31, ADR-008:19-24, `src/protocol/messages.ts:187` and the P3.3 tracker note all describe a response generation; `Catalog.ts:94-183` returns values, not handles, so no handler can know one. The row says "+ vitest project", which names the vitest configuration; the P1.7 and P2.10 rulings (`docs/plans/STATUS.md:492,199`) are the precedent that an answered stop-and-ask is the mechanism for the one more file (`tsconfig.vitest.json`) the row omits, and P0.11 made type-checking the tests a gate. The real root is the only composition that can show what the P1.7 ruling asked for: `refreshProjectsAndSession`, the coalesced reruns and the `session.onDidChange` trigger live in `src/extension.next.ts:136-189`, not in `src/host`, and the P2.10 handoff (`src/STATUS.md:177-184,269-272`) hands exactly that proof to P2.11. Tracing the race with B's listing held: `apply(B)` commits rev 2 and starts run 1 with `lastReconciledProject = B` (`:138`); `apply(A)` commits rev 3 and sets `rerun` (`:184-188`); run 1 then calls `session.reconcile(projects, [shared])` with B's directory list (`:148`), and `normalizeSource` (`SessionStore.ts:133-142`) turns `private` into `all` because the known set is B's; run 2 lists A's directory but `all` stays. Both surfaces receive rev 2, 3, 4 and end equal to the host, so convergence holds and the P1.7 condition is met; the selection loss is a defect of the kind C-state-core-5 named (source validated against another project's list), it is in a P2.10 file, and fixing it in P2.11 would put a root redesign inside the harness item against plan §2.1; the fix item has the harness to verify both this race and the replacement case the P2.10 note describes (`src/STATUS.md:177-184`). ADR-002:48-62 and ADR-003:17-29 give the properties the other scenarios pin; ADR-009 decisions 2 and 7 (`docs/adr/009-catalog.md:12,17`) explain why a cancelling subscriber sees `cancelled` only when the shared computation ends (`Catalog.ts:125-132,323-331`; `QueryCoordinator.ts:339-341` resolves released handles too). The installed Vitest 5.0.3 advances fake timers inside `vi.waitFor` (`node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.C4tKZ0yW.js:7160`: `if (vi.isFakeTimers()) vi.advanceTimersByTime(interval)`), so D1 needs no sleeping.

R4 latest request wins per slot (`session`, `projects`, `installed`, `allProjects`): a response or chunk whose id is not the latest id issued for that slot is recorded and not applied. R5 `ops/progress` events, stream chunks by id, `ops/completed` events and terminal responses are recorded; `pending()` lists request ids without a terminal response. R6 every inbound and outbound envelope is kept verbatim (`sent`, `received`); other events (`ui/*`, `config/changed`) are recorded only. R7 `generation` on a response is recorded if present and never compared (C-protocol-host-7). `expectState({ selectedProject, selectedSource?, projects, installed, allProjects? })` first `settle()`s, then asserts for every resolved surface: its session equals `services.session.snapshot` in `rev` and values and the surfaces equal each other; its project paths equal `projects` and `(await services.catalog.projects()).map(p => p.path)`; its installed result for the selected project has `fidelity: 'provisional'` and `packages.map(p => `${p.id}@${p.version}`)` equal to the literal `installed` list; `pending()` is empty; and every request id in `sent` has exactly one response envelope in `received` (ADR-007). ### P3.2 — ⚑ ruling: the listbox and row markup, and the twelve primitives (2026-10-13)

Brief: plan §2.4 form, item P3.2, on `labs/2.0` @ `3794311` with nothing written. It set the interaction
model's listbox with row action buttons against axe's `nested-interactive`, `aria-required-children` and
`aria-hidden-focus`, gave four options (listbox with a hidden sibling actions container, grid, plain list,
actions outside the list), and asked for the exact DOM and keyboard contract of `Listbox` and `Row`, how
virtualization reaches the DOM under ADR-006, the other ten primitives, the stylesheet layout, the tests, the
wording of the interaction-model edits and whether the item is split. Answer, verbatim; no sentinel, no frozen
path:

`````text
DECISION: Option 1, sharpened: `role="listbox"` → per row a `role="presentation"` wrapper (nothing on it but `className`, `data-*` and the measure `ref`) holding the focusable `role="option"` and a sibling actions container `aria-hidden="true"` whose `IconButton`s are `tabIndex={-1}` with `onMouseDown` prevented; roving `tabIndex`, one `Listbox` component that is always virtualized (no separate `VirtualList` export), single selection now, every action mirrored by a key the listbox handles and announced through the single `LiveStatus`; per-element numbers reach the DOM only as `--nuiget-*` custom properties through React's `style` prop (ADR-006's named mechanism), never as a layout property. One tracker row P3.2, two green commits in a fixed order (a: `Listbox`, `Row`, `IconButton`, `Badge`, `Spinner`, `LiveStatus`, `primitives.css`, tokens, §5/§8, the stylesheet lint test; b: `SectionHeader`, `EmptyState`, `Skeleton`, `ProgressBar`, `Banner`, `Sash`, the barrel, ARCHITECTURE and the gotcha rows). One stylesheet `src/webview/shared/primitives/primitives.css`, imported by every primitive module and by the barrel. `primitives/index.ts` is created in commit b. Not `OWNER MUST DECIDE`: the owner approved the row that recommends this DOM, no frozen path changes, and `contributes` is untouched.

WHY: The brief describes the tree accurately (checked: `src/webview/shared/**` has only `tokens.css`, `primitives/icons.tsx`, `icons.test.tsx`, `STATUS.md`; `src/test/setup-frontend.ts:6-10` registers the matcher; `vitest.config.mts:36-47,70-80`; `package.json:343,353`; `docs/ux/interaction-model.md:48-63,78-82,106-125`; `src/webview/sidebar/components/PackageRow.tsx:95-137` has the button inside the option; `SectionHeader.tsx:31-44` is a `role="button"` div containing action buttons; `DraggableSash.tsx:92-105` mutates `document.body.style`; `App.tsx:3039-3049` positions rows with inline layout styles). The decision is settled by axe-core 4.12.1's own code, not by its documentation: `getOwnedRoles` (`node_modules/axe-core/axe.js:27366`) drops any child that is not visible to screen readers before it looks at roles, so an `aria-hidden="true"` actions container never reaches `aria-required-children`, and it flattens a child whose role is null or presentational only when that child has no global `aria-*` attribute and no `tabindex`, otherwise the child is pushed as an owned element with a null role and fails as "unallowed"; `getMissingContext` walks through null-role parents, so the option inside the wrapper passes `aria-required-parent`; `noFocusableContentEvaluate` (`nested-interactive`) collects every focusable widget descendant and flags `tabindex < 0` as `notHidden`, so a `tabIndex={-1}` button inside the option still fails, which is why the actions must be a sibling and not merely hidden (the quarry note in brief point 3 is right about that, and this is the negative test); `focusableNotTabbableEvaluate` (`aria-hidden-focus`) reads `tabbableElements` only, so `tabIndex={-1}` buttons pass (brief point 6 is right); `option.allowedAttrs` lists `aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize`, `separator` has `requiredAttrs: ['aria-valuenow']` with `ariaRequiredAttrEvaluate` exempting only non-focusable separators (the Sash is focusable, so it carries the attribute), `progressbar` has `accessibleNameRequired: true`, `listbox` allows `aria-multiselectable` for P5. Roving `tabIndex` over `aria-activedescendant` because §5's "visible on `:focus-within`" needs real focus inside the wrapper, and because P3.5's ExTester tests can read `document.activeElement`; the unmount hazard of a virtual list is closed by a `rangeExtractor` that keeps the active index mounted (`defaultRangeExtractor` is exported, `@tanstack/virtual-core/dist/esm/index.d.ts:36`). Options 2 to 4 contradict the owner-approved model and test ids (§5 and §8 say listbox) or lose selection semantics. ADR-006:22-23 reads "styles are set through the CSSOM (React's `style` prop), never as `<style>` or a `style` attribute in rendered HTML": the `style` prop is the permitted mechanism, the icons lost it in P3.1 because they did not need it; jsdom 30 serializes custom properties (`node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/css/CSSStyleDeclaration-impl.js:140,324`), so the test can read them back. Virtual-core's `observeElementRect` seeds from `getBoundingClientRect` and no-ops without `ResizeObserver`, and `scrollWithAdjustments` optional-calls `scrollTo`, so the real virtualizer runs under jsdom when the test stubs the rects; the 1.x tests mock `useVirtualizer` (`InstalledTab.test.tsx:7-11`), which hides exactly what this item must prove. Two commits in one row have precedent (`2dcd3c6`/`9e2ebbc` for P0.13, `b8bfb9c`/`25e9a82` for P1.3, `e080e1f`/`2f903e7` for P1.6); plan line 208 reserves two sessions for P1.1b alone, so the second commit is not a second row and not a licence for a second session.

4. `Listbox` (`primitives/Listbox.tsx`), generic over `T extends { id: string }`. Props: `items: readonly T[]`, `renderRow: (item: T, list: { index; setSize; active; selected; optionId }) => ReactNode` (returns a `Row`), `label: string` or `labelledBy: string` (one required), `hint: string` (required; the visually hidden sentence naming the keys, composed by the consumer, e.g. "Enter uninstalls. Shift+F10 opens the actions menu."), `testId: string`, `density`, `estimateSize?: number` (default 24 compact, 44 comfortable; note in STATUS that these numbers duplicate the two tokens because JS cannot read a token in jsdom), `overscan?: number` (default 5), `selectedId?: string | null`, `onSelect?(item)`, `onActivate?(item)`, `onSecondaryActivate?(item)`, `onDelete?(item)`, `onContextMenu?(item, anchor: { x: number; y: number })`, `busy?: boolean` (`aria-busy` on the listbox while revalidating), `empty?: ReactNode`. DOM:
   `div.nuiget-listbox-root` (flex column, `min-height: 0`) → `div.nuiget-listbox[role="listbox"][aria-label | aria-labelledby][aria-describedby={hintId}][aria-busy?][data-testid={testId}]` (the scroll element: `flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto`; no `tabIndex`) → `div.nuiget-listbox-sizer` (role-less, no aria; `style` = `cssVars({ '--nuiget-virtual-total': `${getTotalSize()}px` })`) → the rows from `renderRow` for `getVirtualItems()`; after the listbox, `span.nuiget-visually-hidden[id={hintId}]` with `hint`. With zero items the `role="listbox"` element is not rendered; instead `div.nuiget-listbox-empty[tabIndex=-1]` wraps `empty`, and the component focuses it when the list had focus-within (the screen reader reads the empty text; nothing lands on `body`). Virtualizer: `useVirtualizer({ count, getScrollElement, estimateSize: () => estimateSize, overscan, getItemKey: i => items[i].id, measureElement: (el) => el.getBoundingClientRect().height || estimateSize, rangeExtractor: range => { const set = new Set(defaultRangeExtractor(range)); if (activeIndex >= 0 && activeIndex < count) set.add(activeIndex); return [...set].sort((a, b) => a - b); } })`. State: `activeId` (internal, keyed by id so it survives reorders); `selected` is controlled by `selectedId`. Event delegation on the listbox element: `onFocus` (focusin) sets `activeId` from `closest('[data-index]')`; `onClick` on an option → `onSelect(item)`; `onContextMenu` anywhere in a row → `onContextMenu(item, { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY })` with `preventDefault`; `onKeyDown`: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active row by one, Home/End to first/last (each: `preventDefault`, set active, `scrollToIndex(i, { align: 'auto' })`, focus in an effect after render), Enter → `onActivate`, Ctrl+Enter or Meta+Enter → `onSecondaryActivate`, Delete or Meta+Backspace → `onDelete`, Shift+F10 or `key === 'ContextMenu'` → `onContextMenu(item, { x: rect.left, y: rect.bottom })` of the option. Enter, Ctrl+Enter and Delete are ignored when the option has `aria-disabled="true"` (read from the DOM, so Row and Listbox cannot disagree); Space, PageUp/PageDown, type-ahead, Left/Right and Escape are not handled (they bubble; Space and `aria-multiselectable` come with P5's bulk toolbar; design `selectedId` so a `selectedIds` set is additive). Focus effect: on `[activeId, items]`, if the active id vanished, active becomes the item at `min(oldIndex, items.length - 1)`; if the listbox had focus-within, `getElementById(optionId)?.focus({ preventScroll: true })` after `scrollToIndex`.
5. `IconButton`: `button.nuiget-icon-button[type="button"][aria-label={label}][title={label}][aria-pressed?][disabled?][tabIndex?][data-testid?]` with the icon child `aria-hidden`; `label` required; `min-width`/`min-height: var(--nuiget-target-min)`. `Badge`: `span.nuiget-badge.nuiget-badge--{tone}` with `label`; when `title` is given, `span[aria-hidden="true"]{label}` + `span.nuiget-visually-hidden{title}` so the row description reads "Centrally managed", not "CPM"; no `aria-label` on a span (axe `aria-prohibited-attr`). `Spinner`: `span.nuiget-spinner` around `LoadingIcon` with `title={label}` (named → `role="img"`; unnamed → `aria-hidden`), animation `nuiget-spin calc(var(--nuiget-duration-normal) * 5) linear infinite`.
6. `LiveStatus`: `div.nuiget-visually-hidden[role="status"][aria-live="polite"][aria-atomic="true"][data-testid="status-live"]`, prop `message: string | null`, mounted from the first render of the surface (a live region announces changes only); an identical consecutive message is re-announced by clearing the text and setting it on the next animation frame. No queue and no store (P3.3): it shows the latest message. The shell does not duplicate `Banner` text into it.
7. `SectionHeader`: `div.nuiget-section-header` → `h2|h3` (`level` prop, default 2) → `button.nuiget-section-toggle[type="button"][aria-expanded][aria-controls={contentId}][data-testid=`section-header-${testKey}`]` holding `ChevronRightIcon` (aria-hidden, rotated by CSS when expanded), `span.nuiget-section-title[id]` and, when `count !== undefined`, a `Badge`; `busy` renders a decorative `Spinner` inside the button; `actions` render in a sibling `div.nuiget-section-actions` after the heading, never inside the button (1.x's `role="button"` div with buttons inside is the `nested-interactive` the item exists to remove). The title span's `id` is what a `Listbox` passes as `labelledBy`. `EmptyState`: `div.nuiget-empty[data-testid?]` → `p.nuiget-empty-text{message}` + optional `button.nuiget-button[type="button"]{action.label}`; no role, no `tabIndex` (the focus target is the Listbox's container around it). `Skeleton`: `div.nuiget-skeleton[aria-hidden="true"]` with `rows` (default 3) × `div.nuiget-skeleton-row.nuiget-skeleton-row--{density}`; no text, no role: the "Loading …" of §4 is the `LiveStatus` message. `ProgressBar`: `div.nuiget-progress[.nuiget-progress--indeterminate][role="progressbar"][aria-label={label}][aria-valuemin="0"][aria-valuemax="100"][aria-valuenow={value} only when determinate]` → `div.nuiget-progress-bar`; `style` = `cssVars({ '--nuiget-progress-value': `${value}%` })` when determinate; `label` required. `Banner`: `div.nuiget-banner.nuiget-banner--{severity}[role={severity === 'error' ? 'alert' : 'status'}][data-testid?]` → severity icon (aria-hidden), `span.nuiget-visually-hidden{`${Severity}: `}`, `span.nuiget-banner-text{children}`, optional `button.nuiget-button.nuiget-button--secondary[type="button"]{action.label}`; a second `role="status"` is acceptable here because the message must announce when it appears (WCAG 4.1.3); P3.4 tests scope `getByRole('status')` by test id. `Sash`: `div.nuiget-sash.nuiget-sash--{orientation}[role="separator"][tabIndex=0][aria-orientation][aria-valuenow={value}][aria-valuemin={min}][aria-valuemax={max}][aria-label={label}][aria-controls?][data-testid="sash"]`; props `value`, `min` (20), `max` (80), `defaultValue` (50), `step` (1), `orientation`, `label`, `onChange(value)`, `onChangeEnd?(value)`; keys: the two arrows along the axis ±step, Shift+arrow ±10·step, Home → min, End → max, Enter → `defaultValue` (keyboard twin of double-click, WCAG 2.5.7); pointer: Pointer Events with `setPointerCapture`, percent from `parentElement.getBoundingClientRect()`, clamped, `touch-action: none` and the cursor in CSS; the sash renders no `style`: the parent sets `--nuiget-split` on its layout container with `cssVars`. The hit area is widened to 24 px with a `::after` overlay around a 4 px visual.
8. `primitives.css`: class prefix `nuiget-`, BEM-lite modifiers (`--compact`, `--busy`, `--error`); `.nuiget-visually-hidden` (clip pattern) once; rows: `.nuiget-listbox-sizer { position: relative; height: var(--nuiget-virtual-total) }`, `.nuiget-row { position: absolute; inset: 0 auto auto 0; width: 100%; transform: translateY(var(--nuiget-virtual-offset)) }`, `.nuiget-row-actions { visibility: hidden }`, `.nuiget-row:hover .nuiget-row-actions, .nuiget-row:focus-within .nuiget-row-actions, .nuiget-row--busy .nuiget-row-actions { visibility: visible }`; focus ring `.nuiget-row-option:focus-visible, .nuiget-icon-button:focus-visible, .nuiget-sash:focus-visible, .nuiget-section-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--nuiget-color-focus); outline-offset: -1px }` (an outline, not a shadow, so it survives forced colours; the token is already `Highlight` there); `forced-color-adjust: none` only on `.nuiget-row-option[aria-selected="true"]`, `.nuiget-badge` and `.nuiget-progress-bar`, whose tokens already map to system colours; every duration is a `var(--nuiget-duration-*)` or a `calc()` of one; no `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)`, no `!important`, no `px` font size, no colour literal. Every primitive module has `import './primitives.css'`; the barrel imports it too.
9. Tests, frontend project, one `*.test.tsx` per primitive, each ending with `has no axe violations` on its own render. Titles the gate should read: `Row`: `the option is named by id and version and described by badges and status`, `the row wrapper carries no aria attribute and no tabindex`, `the actions container is hidden from assistive technology and its buttons are not tabbable`, `clicking an action keeps focus on the option`, `a busy row is aria-busy and shows a spinner instead of its actions`, `a disabled row renders no actions`, `the only inline style is the virtual offset custom property`. `Listbox`: `renders rows as options with posinset and setsize`, `ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End move the active option and the roving tabindex`, `Enter activates, Ctrl+Enter and Meta+Enter are the secondary action`, `Delete and Meta+Backspace delete the active item`, `Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key report the active item with an anchor`, `right-click on a row reports the item`, `a disabled option ignores Enter, Ctrl+Enter and Delete but keeps focus and the context menu`, `the active row follows its id when items reorder`, `when the active item disappears focus moves to the row at its index`, `when the list empties the empty container takes focus`, `only the rows in view plus overscan are rendered, and the active row stays mounted off-screen` (stub `vi.spyOn(Element.prototype, 'getBoundingClientRect')` keyed on `this`: `[role="listbox"]` → the viewport height, `[data-index]` → the row height, installed before render; never mock `useVirtualizer`), `the only inline styles are the virtual total and offsets`, `a listbox with rows, badges and actions has no axe violations`. Negative, in `Listbox.test.tsx`, each asserting `violations.map(v => v.id)` contains the rule: `a button inside an option is a nested-interactive violation` (also with `tabindex="-1"`), `a wrapper with aria-busy between listbox and option is an aria-required-children violation`, `a tabbable button under aria-hidden is an aria-hidden-focus violation`. `IconButton`: `has the accessible name it is given`, `passes tabIndex, pressed and disabled through`. `Badge`: `reads its title to assistive technology when one is given`. `Spinner`: `is decorative without a label and an image with one`. `LiveStatus`: `is a polite atomic status region with the test id`, `re-announces an identical message`. `SectionHeader`: `is a heading with a toggle button that reports aria-expanded and aria-controls`, `actions are outside the button`, `the count renders as a badge`. `EmptyState`: `renders the sentence and the optional action`. `Skeleton`: `renders the number of rows asked and is hidden from assistive technology`. `ProgressBar`: `determinate exposes the value, indeterminate omits aria-valuenow`, `the only inline style is the progress custom property`. `Banner`: `warning and info are status, error is alert`, `the severity is spoken before the text`, `the action is a button`. `Sash`: `is a focusable separator with value, min, max and orientation`, `arrows, Shift+arrows, Home, End and Enter change the value within the clamps`, `dragging reports clamped percentages and the end value`, `renders no inline style`. Plus `primitives/composed.test.tsx`: `SectionHeader, Listbox with three rows and actions, Banner and LiveStatus together have no axe violations`.
10. Interaction model edits (`docs/ux/interaction-model.md`). Replace the §5 keyboard paragraph (lines 78-82) with: "Keyboard: every pointer action is reachable by keyboard. A list is a `role="listbox"` whose rows are `role="option"` with roving `tabIndex` (one tab stop per list; the active row has `tabIndex=0`). ArrowUp/ArrowDown move, Home/End jump to the first and last row; moving changes the active row, not the selection. Enter activates the row (main panel: selects it and shows its details; sidebar: performs its primary action), Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) performs the secondary action, Delete (Cmd+Backspace on macOS) uninstalls where applicable, and Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key opens the actions menu for the active row; right-click anywhere on the row opens the same menu. Row action buttons are pointer-only: they sit next to the option in a container hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden="true"`, `tabIndex={-1}`), become visible on `:hover` and `:focus-within` of the row, and clicking one keeps focus on the row. Each listbox describes its keys in a visually hidden sentence (`aria-describedby`); outcomes are announced through the one `role="status"` region (`status-live`). A row with a pending operation is `aria-busy="true"`, its status text is part of its description and a spinner replaces its actions. A disabled row (`aria-disabled="true"`, e.g. unresolved) keeps focus, selection and the context menu but ignores Enter, Ctrl+Enter and Delete. When the active row disappears, focus moves to the row now at its index (or the last one); when the list empties, the empty-state container takes focus." Note in the STATUS that Cmd+Backspace is an addition over 1.x (`SidebarApp.tsx:1142` handled `Delete` only) and that Space, PageUp/PageDown and multi-selection are reserved for P5. §8: change the `package-row-<id>` cell to "A row (id lower-cased): the wrapper around the option and its pointer actions; the option is the `role="option"` inside it (read `aria-selected` there)"; add `row-action-<name>` | "A pointer action button inside a row (`install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `more`); hidden from assistive technology, mirrored by the keys of §5"; add `section-header-<name>` | "The toggle button of a collapsible section (`installed`, `updates`)"; `status-live` and `sash` unchanged. §4 needs no edit: "Skeleton rows (3) + `role="status"` text" is the Skeleton plus the `LiveStatus` message.

### P3.5 — stop-and-ask: putting a 2.0 build under the e2e and ExTester suites (2026-10-13)

Brief: plan §2.4 form, item P3.5, on `labs/2.0` @ `8c95e9e` with nothing written. The row names two test files
and `ci.yml`. In the tree, `.vscode-test.mjs` has one configuration whose glob would run a new `v2-*` e2e file
in the existing 1.x `E2E` jobs; `vsce` and ExTester always run `vscode:prepublish`, which builds the 1.x
entries over whatever `--v2` wrote, so no existing script yields a 2.0 VSIX; `check:vsix` requires
`dist/webview.css`, which a `--v2` build does not have (N62); the fixture project is shared with the 1.x
suites; an extension-host test cannot see the webview. It asked which files beyond the three may change and by
which mechanism the two jobs get the 2.0 entries, what each suite asserts, which fixture, what happens to
`check:vsix`, the shape of the jobs and how a red run of a new job counts. Answer, verbatim; no sentinel, no
frozen path:

`````text
DECISION: Option 1, narrowed: one environment switch, `NUIGET_V2=1`, read by `esbuild.mjs` and by `.vscode-test.mjs`; one new npm script (`test:ui:v2`; the env switch makes `npm run test:e2e` select the v2 suite, so no e2e script is added); the two new CI jobs set the variable at job level; the shared fixture is kept and restored; `check:vsix` is not run on a 2.0 build. Not `OWNER MUST DECIDE`: every file this touches is tooling, and `package.json` `contributes` stays untouched (§2.3).

WHY: The brief is right about the tree. `vsce` always runs `vscode:prepublish` (`node_modules/@vscode/vsce/out/package.js:1561`, unconditional in `packageCommand`; `createVSIX` at `api.js:25` calls the same function, so ExTester's `--package_options` cannot skip it), and the prepublish child is spawned with `shell: true` and no `env` override (`package.js:1477`), so an environment variable is the one switch that reaches `npm run package` → `node esbuild.mjs --production` inside both `npx vsce package` and `extest setup-and-run`. `.vscode-test.mjs` has exactly one configuration and already reads `process.env.VSCODE_TEST_VERSION` (`.vscode-test.mjs:7`), so an env-selected `files` pattern follows the file's own precedent; `@vscode/test-cli` expands `files` with `glob()` and supports no negation (`node_modules/@vscode/test-cli/out/cli/gatherFiles.mjs:10-18`), so the legacy pattern must exclude `v2-*` by extglob. the client model and not the slices) and the five decisions earlier rows handed to P3.6 (N63, N61, N64, the compact
row, the `src/webview/**` coverage ratchet), with three estimate options and four ordering options, unpicked. It
asked for the re-based estimate with its unit, the ordering and row splits, and the ruling on each handed decision
with the item and files that carry it. Answer, verbatim; no sentinel, no frozen path:

DECISION: Re-base in measured hours, not session-days; reorder so that P5.1, P5.3 and P5.4 run before P4.1 and P4 then runs whole; dissolve P5.2 into the feature rows (the row stays as a closing sweep, never `skipped`); split P5.12 into P5.12a (e2e ports) and P5.12b (ExTester gap-fill, retirement map, CI shape); from P5.4 on every feature row adds its own ExTester test. ### P4.1 — ⚑ proxy and certificate matrix before Transport (2026-10-14)

Brief: plan §2.4 form, item P4.1, on `labs/2.0` @ `18fe2cd` with nothing written. It pasted the facts F1-F8 that a
research subagent of the session read at VS Code 1.85.0 / `@vscode/proxy-agent` 0.18.2 and at the current release
(with their citations), the quarry's `Transport.ts` and `proxyConfigured()` excerpts, ADR-005's `Transport` bullet,
and twelve options unpicked (HTTP/1.1 path A/B/C, HTTP/2 D/E/F, vendoring G/H, settings I/J, contract text K/L).
Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: HTTP/1.1 = A (no agent of our own; the host patch does the proxying); HTTP/2 = E sharpened (allow-listed origins only, gated by the injected predicate `http.proxySupport !== 'off' && (http.proxy set || HTTPS_PROXY/https_proxy/HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy set)`, with a connection-level failure downgrading the origin to HTTP/1.1 for the lifetime of the `Transport` instance instead of the quarry's 60 s cooldown); vendoring = G (none); settings = J (`http.proxyStrictSSL` and `http.proxyAuthorization` are stated as not applied, never emulated, certificate verification never disabled); contract text = K (amend ADR-005 and write `docs/adr/005-proxy-matrix.md` as a supplement; `src/core/contracts.ts` is not touched). Nothing in this item is OWNER MUST DECIDE: no `contributes` change, no dependency added, no release or scope question; the plan row itself delegates the vendoring decision to P4.1 with advisor sign-off.

WHY: The brief is wrong about the tree in one place, and it matters: `src/core/contracts.ts:254-258` does not mention `http.proxyStrictSSL`. It says "Honours VS Code proxy settings by routing HTTP/1.1 through Node's `https` module (which the extension host patches for proxies); HTTP/2 is used only when no proxy is configured", which stays true under this ruling, so option L dissolves and D6 stays narrow (P4.1 is named for `docs/adr/**` only, plan line 50). The brief is right about `docs/adr/005-execution-context-and-outbound-policy.md:30-36` (names `http.proxyStrictSSL`, and the P1.1b diff review at `docs/plans/STATUS.md:740` already left the dropped "falls back to HTTP/1.1" clause to P4.1), about the three `REMOVAL GATE: P4.9` anchors in `src/extension.next.ts:72,205,274`, about the P4.2/P4.9 tracker notes (`docs/plans/STATUS.md:64,71`) and about `src/core/http` holding only `ssrf.ts`, `index.ts`, tests and the P1.9 note. On the facts F1-F8 I have no outside access and could not verify them; they are consistent with each other and with the GitLab and C# extension behaviour the subagent cites, and the ruling rests on two of them (F2, F4), which DO step 3 makes the session re-read at the pinned tags before writing. Given F4, the choice on the HTTP/1.1 path is decided by `http.proxySupport: on`, not by keep-alive: under `override` (the default) a caller-supplied agent is discarded anyway, and under `on` a defined agent bypasses the proxy entirely, which is a correctness failure for exactly the corporate users the plan's §7 risk row ("Transport/proxy regresses corporate users | P4.1 before P4.2; HTTP/2 only without proxy", plan line 358) protects; passing no agent is correct in all four modes and the only cost is keep-alive on Node 18 hosts (D10 baseline), which Node 19 and later hosts restore through the global agent. Given F3, the HTTP/2 predicate cannot see an operating-system or PAC proxy or a TLS-intercepting CA, so the h2→h1 fallback is the real safety net and must be sticky: a 60 s cooldown against a connect that times out under a dropping firewall is a recurring stall. Dropping HTTP/2 (option D) would reopen the plan's own mitigation and the P4.2 row's test list ("h2→h1 fallback", plan line 258), so it is not taken. Vendoring an agent is reached only when the user has set `http.proxySupport: off`, where honouring `http.proxy` would contradict the user's own setting, is replaced by the host under `override` (F4), loses PAC, OS proxy, Kerberos and OS certificates (F7), and adds a dependency with Node 18 version ceilings; so none. Emulating `http.proxyStrictSSL` would mean `rejectUnauthorized: false` from a setting VS Code itself scopes to its own request service (F2), which `.github/instructions/security-and-owasp.instructions.md` forbids; the dotnet CLI does not read VS Code settings either, so J loses no parity.

### P4.6 — stop-and-ask: CLI search output, return shape, search policy, icons (2026-10-15)

Brief: the row's "CLI JSON extraction after `warn :` lines" rests on an untracked quarry claim that six captures on macOS
SDK 10.0.401 did not reproduce; `SearchClient.search` cannot carry `sourcesUnavailable`; which sources a free-text query and
an id lookup may reach; whether rows keep a remote `iconUrl`. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: One ruling, composed from options 1, 3, 4 and 5 and sharpened: `search.ts` extracts the JSON document tolerantly from `dotnet package search` stdout (never `JSON.parse(stdout)`), the seven captures are promoted to a tracked, redacted fixture under `src/core/feeds/__fixtures__/cli-search/` with one labelled-synthetic prefix-line case and one `NUIGET_SDK_TESTS`-gated real-CLI test; `SearchClient.search` returns `{ results, sourcesUnavailable: boolean }` and `searchById` answers `found | missing | failed` (the `IconFetch` shape); a free-text query goes to every source the client is handed, unfiltered, while anything that sends a package id (`exactMatch`, `searchById`, `lookup`) passes the outbound policy first; nothing defaults to nuget.org or recognises it by address; results carry no `iconUrl`. Not OWNER MUST DECIDE.

WHY: The brief holds against the tree with one sharpening: the quarry claim is at `git show f837f34:src/core/feeds/STATUS.md:31`, the quarry has no `search.ts` at that commit (only `STATUS.md`, `icons.ts`, `wire.ts` under feeds), and nothing in `src/core`, `src/host` or `src/extension.next.ts` implements or consumes `SearchClient`/`SearchByIdClient` yet, so the declarations at `src/core/feeds/types.ts:65-71,157-159` are this item's own unfrozen surface and changing them loses no work. (a) The `warn :` claim is unreproduced on macOS 10.0.401 and rests only on a gitignored capture (plan §2.6 forbids citing it), but the tracked probe `src/core/cli/__fixtures__/sdk-probes/10.0.401.json:37,72,135` proves this SDK does write `info :`/`warn :` lines to stdout in some environments, and your captures 3-6 prove failures arrive as structured `problems[]` (exit 0 per source, exit 1 top-level for an HTTP source) which 1.x's `JSON.parse(stdout)` at `src/services/NuGetPackageService.ts:885` would read correctly only while no prefix line appears; tolerant extraction covers both worlds at no cost, so option 2 is wrong and option 1 is right once the synthetic case is built from the tracked probe's text rather than the quarry's wording. (b) `PackageSearchResult[]` cannot carry "a source did not answer"; the gotcha "Empty is not unknown", ADR-009 (`docs/adr/009-catalog.md:24`), `Catalog.ts:77-81` and the sibling `UpdateChecker.check` at `types.ts:122` (`{ updates; sourcesUnavailable: boolean }`) all want the flag at the client, and the same hole exists for `searchById`, whose `undefined` the quarry note (`:33`) and P4.7/P4.8 would read as "no such id" after a transport failure; `IconFetch` at `types.ts:100-103` is the house answer. `quickSearch` keeps `QuickSearchSourceResult[]`: the frozen `search/autocomplete` result (`src/protocol/messages.ts:133`) has no `sourcesUnavailable` and a group is simply absent. (c) ADR-005 (`005-execution-context-and-outbound-policy.md:29-31,54`) keys the policy on a package id; a free-text query is not one, but `packageid:<query>` (`NuGetPackageService.ts:709`), `searchById` and `lookup` are, so they go through `filterAllowedSources`/`allowedSourcesFor` inside the client as `icons.ts:144` does. The nuget.org default of 1.x (`:550-552`, `:2215`) and its address test (`:564`) are ledger M2 ("quick-search default") and contradict `DefaultOutboundPolicy`'s "No source is treated specially by its address"; the P4 gate requires the M2 test present. The row-level filter of free-text results (your 4-ii) is a policy edge case the plan marks ⚑ at P4.8; it is deferred there explicitly, not decided silently. (d) ADR-006 (`006-icons-and-csp.md:16-19`) puts icons host-side as `data:` URIs; a remote URL in `iconUrl` would never render and would leak the flat-container pattern of 1.x `:794-802`; the `search/query` `metadata` chunk (`messages.ts:132`) is where data URIs arrive (P4.8 enricher, P4.9 wiring). One more frozen sentence shapes the merge: `src/protocol/domain.ts:92` says `sourceUrl` is the "first source when merged", so the merge keeps the first-listed source's entry (deterministic in config order) and drops 1.x's "higher download count wins" heuristic; no deviation to record.
