### P4.8 — ⚑ policy edge cases of updates, enrichment and metadata (2026-10-16)

Brief: nine questions (Q1-Q9): free-text search rows and the vulnerability lookup under the mapping (deferred from P4.6
and P4.7), update racing, empty vs unknown per package, bare rows vs inline enrichment, enricher sources, the metadata
chain and its offline fallback, the versions return shape, and what the private-only and F6 tests assert. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: One ruling for Q1-Q9, none of them the owner's. Q1 (a): every free-text search row is kept; nothing filters rows by `allowedSourcesFor(row.id, [rowSource])`, at the client or in the Catalog. Q2 (a): advisories from every handed-in source's vulnerability data apply to every id. Q3 (b): `check` waits for every allowed source of a package and takes the newest version across them; `sourceUrl` is the source that has it, ties go to the first-listed source. Q4 (a): `sourcesUnavailable` is true when any allowed source of any candidate package answered `undefined`, whether or not another source produced an update; a package whose allowed set is empty is skipped and leaves the flag alone; comparison is against `effectiveInstalledVersion(parseVersionSpec(pkg.version), pkg.resolvedVersion)`, gated by `isUpdateCandidate`, `declaration: 'unresolved'` skipped, `isImplicit` not skipped (parity with 1.x; the surface decides what it offers). Q5 (a): `check` returns bare rows (`id`, `installedVersion` = the effective installed version, `latestVersion`, `sourceUrl`); the enricher adds `iconUrl`/`verified`/`authors` separately and the Catalog composes the two at P4.9. Q6 (a): `lookup` on the allowed sources in source order, first answer wins; icons through the injected `IconResolver` (filters inside); vulnerabilities through `VulnerabilityClient.forPackage` over every handed-in source, `vulnerabilities` absent when it answers `sourcesUnavailable`, `[]` when it answered with none; per-package isolation and a named concurrency bound; no lite cache inside the enricher in P4.8 (the `lite` cache kind of `CachePolicy` is wired at P4.9 together with the coordinator's treatment of the metadata chunk). Q7 (b): per allowed source in order, registration → flat-container nuspec → `searchById` lite fields, first source with an answer wins and carries its `sourceUrl`; the offline reader runs whenever no allowed source produced metadata, for any reason, including an empty allowed set; no cache and no in-flight dedupe inside the resolver. Q8: `MetadataResolver.versions` returns `{ versions: string[]; sourcesUnavailable: boolean }` (a `VersionsOutcome` in `types.ts`, the module's own surface): union over the allowed sources, deduplicated by normalized version, `sortDescending`, the flag set when any allowed source answered `undefined`; `readme` is `ReadmeExtractor.extract` over `filterAllowedSources(policy, id, sources)`. Q9: one new feeds-level test file with two configurations, the literally titled `private-only configuration never contacts nuget.org` (nuget.org never handed in, no mapping) asserting zero nuget.org hosts across every entry point, and a second test (nuget.org handed in as an enabled source, a mapping that sends every id to the private feed) asserting that no request to a nuget.org host carries the package id in its path or query; the pair closes M2. The F6 test lives in `metadataResolver.test.ts`. Not OWNER MUST DECIDE.

WHY: The brief holds against the tree with one correction and two hazards. Correction: 1.x updates do race (`src/services/NuGetPackageService.ts:295-316` with `raceForFirstResultWithIndex` at `:1437-1475`, first non-empty list wins, `.catch(() => [])` turns a dead feed into "no update") and compare `versions[0]` with `pkg.version`, the spec text (`:2072-2077`), and `getPackageSearchMetadata` is hard-wired to `https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json` (`:2215`, ledger M2 at `docs/plans/findings-ledger.md:200`); but the 2.0 `FlatContainerClient` applies no policy at all (`grep -n policy src/core/feeds/flatContainer.ts` → nothing; `icons.ts:144` and `registration.ts:127,152` filter before calling it, `readme.ts:90` says "already policy-filtered"), so the resolver's direct `flat.nuspec` and any `flat.packageSize` call must run on a filtered list or P4.8 reintroduces the leak the M2 row names for `getPackageSize`. ADR-005 (`docs/adr/005-execution-context-and-outbound-policy.md:29-31,54`) keys the policy on a package id being sent to a source and on nuget.org being an enabled source: a free-text row's id was never sent anywhere, so dropping it protects nothing and hides a result a feed the user configured returned (NuGet's own tooling does not filter search results by mapping; mapping decides where restore fetches a package), while the follow-up enrichment of those rows is id-bearing and goes through the policy in the enricher and the icon resolver (Q1); the vulnerability download sends no id (`vulnerability.ts:4,108-124`) and goes only to the sources handed in, so applying every source's data to every id keeps both ADR sentences, matches NuGet audit's behaviour and keeps advisories for the common mirror set-up (`*` mapped to a proxy without a `VulnerabilityInfo` resource), at the residual cost of an id collision between a private and a public package that the version-range match limits (Q2). Q4(a) forces Q3(b): the flag cannot be computed without waiting for every allowed source, and `RegistrationClient.versions` already answers `undefined` (failed) versus `[]` (unknown or refused) (`registration.ts:122-129`), so the gotcha "Empty is not unknown", ADR-009 (`docs/adr/009-catalog.md:24`) and `UpdatesQueryResult.sourcesUnavailable` (`src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts:63-67`) are served; `isUpdateCandidate`/`effectiveInstalledVersion` (`src/core/versioning/VersionRange.ts:279-302`) exist for exactly this gating and close N6 (exact pins never candidates); `isNewer` is false for an unparsable installed version (`NuGetVersion.ts:164-166`). The protocol already separates rows from decoration: `updates/get` streams `{ kind: 'found'; update }` and `allProjects/updates` has a separate `icons` chunk (`src/protocol/messages.ts:122,128`), and `installed/get` and `search/query` deliver lite metadata as a `metadata` chunk (`:121,132`), so bare rows plus a separate enricher is the shape the frozen contract expects (Q5, Q6). Q7(b) is the only implementable choice: `RegistrationClient.metadata` and `FlatContainerClient.nuspec` return `undefined` for unknown, refused and failed alike (`registration.ts:149-170`, `types.ts:96,101`), so the resolver cannot tell "every source unreachable" from "no source knows it"; `OfflineMetadataReader.metadata` already marks `offline: true` and is never cached (`offline.ts:58-96`). That contradicts the frozen JSDoc at `src/protocol/domain.ts:130-131` ("because every source was unreachable"); it is recorded as a deviation, not hidden and not edited. F6 (`findings-ledger.md:234`) was an inner cache keyed `${id}@${version}` without the source (`NuGetPackageService.ts:1700`); a resolver without any cache, answering with the winning source's `sourceUrl`, cannot bleed, and `cacheKeys.metadata`/`versions` already carry the source (`src/core/cache/CachePolicy.ts:109-116`). The hazard moves one layer up: `resourceKeys.metadata(id, version, undefined)` and `resourceKeys.versions(id, undefined, pre)` key on `'all'` (`domain.ts:234-237`) with no project, while the answer depends on the project's source list and mapping; that is P4.9's problem (frozen key shape), recorded below as a new finding. Q8: the house shape since the P4.6 ruling (`docs/plans/STATUS.md:1955`) is an outcome object with the flag; `package/versions` carries none (`messages.ts:136`), so the Catalog maps it at P4.9, the resolver does not decide. `DefaultOutboundPolicy` treats no address specially (`src/core/sources/DefaultOutboundPolicy.ts:5-9`) and its own test `private-only configuration never yields nuget.org` (`DefaultOutboundPolicy.test.ts:89`) proves the policy; the plan row (`docs/plans/2026-10-11-nuiget-2.0-execution-plan.md:264`) and the P4 gate (`:268`) want the feeds-level proof that the clients obey it, which is the named test.

DO:
1. `src/core/feeds/types.ts` (unfrozen, no sentinel): add `export interface VersionsOutcome { versions: string[]; /** True when an allowed source could not answer; the list may be incomplete. False with `[]` means no allowed source has the package, or none was allowed. */ sourcesUnavailable: boolean }` and change `MetadataResolver.versions(...)` to `Promise<VersionsOutcome>`. Extend the `UpdateChecker.check` JSDoc with: exact pins and invalid specs are never candidates (`isUpdateCandidate`), the installed version compared and reported is `effectiveInstalledVersion`, implicit references are checked like any other, and `sourcesUnavailable` is true when any allowed source of any candidate answered `undefined` or the check was cancelled. Extend `MetadataResolver.metadata`'s JSDoc: "first allowed source in order; offline when no allowed source produced metadata, for any reason". No other declaration changes.
2. `src/core/feeds/updates.ts`: `export class DefaultUpdateChecker implements UpdateChecker` with `constructor(deps: Pick<FeedsDeps, 'policy' | 'logger'>, registration: RegistrationClient, options?: { concurrency?: number })`, `export const UPDATE_CHECK_CONCURRENCY = 16`. Per installed package, in input order with bounded concurrency and a per-package try/catch (a rejection is logged redacted and counts as `undefined` from that package's sources; `batchedPromiseAll` of `src/core/util/concurrency.ts:14-45` rethrows the first rejection after the batch, so either wrap each worker or use `mapWithConcurrency` from `wire.ts`): skip when `declaration === 'unresolved'`; `spec = parseVersionSpec(pkg.version)`; skip when `!isUpdateCandidate(spec, pkg.resolvedVersion)`; `installed = effectiveInstalledVersion(spec, pkg.resolvedVersion)`, skip when undefined; `allowed = filterAllowedSources(policy, pkg.id, sources)`, skip when empty (flag unchanged); ask every allowed source `registration.versions(source, pkg.id, { includePrerelease, listedOnly: true, signal })` concurrently and wait for all; any `undefined` → `unavailable = true`; from the answers take each source's first element (they are sorted descending), pick the greatest by `compareText`, ties to the first-listed source; when `isNewer(candidate, installed)` build `{ id: pkg.id, installedVersion: installed, latestVersion: candidate, sourceUrl: winner.source.url }`, call `onFound`, collect. Return `{ updates }` in installed order (not completion order) and `sourcesUnavailable: unavailable || signal?.aborted === true`. No icon, lookup or vulnerability call in this file; no `versionType` switch (parse the spec text); the string `nuget.org` appears nowhere in the file.
3. `src/core/feeds/enricher.ts`: `export class DefaultMetadataEnricher implements MetadataEnricher` with `constructor(deps: Pick<FeedsDeps, 'policy' | 'logger'>, search: Pick<SearchClient, 'lookup'>, icons: IconResolver, vulnerabilities: VulnerabilityClient, options?: { concurrency?: number })`, `export const ENRICH_CONCURRENCY = 8`. One `PackageMetadataLite` per asked package, in input order, always echoing the asked `id` and `version` (never the version `lookup` returns). Per package, isolated by try/catch: `allowed = filterAllowedSources(policy, id, sources)`; `lookup(source, id, signal)` over `allowed` in order, first defined answer supplies `verified`, `authors`, `description`; `iconUrl = await icons.icon(sources, id, version, signal)` (the resolver filters by policy itself); `const v = await vulnerabilities.forPackage(sources, id, version, signal)` over every handed-in source, `lite.vulnerabilities = v.vulnerabilities` unless `v.sourcesUnavailable`, in which case the field stays absent. Run `lookup`, icon and vulnerabilities of one package concurrently. No cache in this file, no `searchById` unless the found/missing/failed distinction is needed (it is not for best-effort lite data), no `nuget.org`.
4. `src/core/feeds/metadataResolver.ts`: `export class DefaultMetadataResolver implements MetadataResolver` with `constructor(deps: Pick<FeedsDeps, 'policy' | 'logger'>, clients: { registration: RegistrationClient; flat: FlatContainerClient; search: SearchByIdClient; readme: ReadmeExtractor; offline: OfflineMetadataReader })`. `metadata(sources, id, version, signal)`: `allowed = filterAllowedSources(policy, id, sources)`; for each allowed source in order and stop at the first answer: `registration.metadata(source, id, version, signal)`; else when `source.endpoints.packageBaseAddress`, `flat.nuspec(source, id, version, signal)` → `parseNuspec` → `nuspecToMetadata(nuspec, { sourceUrl: source.source.url })`; else when `source.endpoints.searchQueryService`, `search.searchById(source, id, true, signal)` and on `found` a `PackageMetadata` from the row (`id`, `version` = the asked version, `description`, `authors`, `totalDownloads`, `dependencies: []`, `sourceUrl`); `packageSize`, if filled at all, from the winning source's flat container only, best effort. When no allowed source produced metadata (including `allowed.length === 0`): `return offline.metadata(id, version)` (already `offline: true`). No cache, no in-flight map: the coordinator dedupes and caches at P4.9. `versions(sources, id, options)`: `allowed` as above; empty → `{ versions: [], sourcesUnavailable: false }`; else `registration.versions(source, id, options)` on every allowed source concurrently; `versions` = the union deduplicated by `normalize(text)` keeping the first text seen in source order, then `sortDescending`; `sourcesUnavailable` = any answer `undefined`. `readme(sources, id, version, signal)`: `readme.extract(filterAllowedSources(policy, id, sources), id, version, signal)`. Export a pure `searchResultToMetadata(row: PackageSearchResult, version: string): PackageMetadata` for its own test.
5. `src/core/feeds/index.ts`: `export * from './updates'; export * from './enricher'; export * from './metadataResolver';` (`testSupport.ts` stays unexported).
6. Tests, all with `FakeTransport` from `testSupport.ts` and real clients (`DefaultRegistrationClient` over `DefaultSearchClient` and `DefaultFlatContainerClient`) where the interaction matters, fakes implementing the `types.ts` interfaces where it does not. `updates.test.ts`: `skips unresolved declarations, invalid specs, exact pins and floating or range specs without a resolved version (N6)`; `compares against the resolved version of a floating spec and reports it as installedVersion`; `takes the newest version across every allowed source and names the source that has it, ties to the first-listed source`; `waits for every allowed source instead of the first non-empty answer`; `reports sourcesUnavailable when an allowed source failed even though another source produced an update`; `does not report sourcesUnavailable for an unknown package or a package no source is allowed for`; `never sends the nuspec or size request to a source the policy refuses` (flat container has no policy of its own); `falls back to the offline nuspec when no allowed source produced metadata, also when none is allowed, and marks it offline`; DO NOT:
- Do not filter free-text search rows by the policy anywhere, and do not record the row's source as a reason to drop it.
- Do not restrict advisories to the sources the mapping allows for an id; do not hand `forPackage` a policy-filtered list.
- Do not take the first source whose list is non-empty (1.x racing), and do not read `versions[0]` of one source without comparing across the allowed sources.
- Do not compare against `pkg.version` (the spec text) or branch on `pkg.versionType`; parse the spec and use `effectiveInstalledVersion`.
- Do not treat an empty allowed set, an unknown package or a refused source as `sourcesUnavailable`; only `undefined` answers and cancellation set it.
- Do not call `flat.nuspec`, `flat.packageSize` or `flat.versionIndex` on an unfiltered source list.
- Do not add a cache, an in-flight map or a `${id}@${version}` key of any kind to `updates.ts`, `enricher.ts` or `metadataResolver.ts`.
- Do not enrich inside `check`, and do not call the icon resolver, `lookup` or the vulnerability client from `updates.ts`.
- Do not change the asked `version` on a lite entry to the version a search answered.

### P4.9 — stop-and-ask: wiring the feeds (2026-10-16)

Brief: how P4.9 wires the feeds (deps shape, per-context policy and credentials, the project context of reads without a
project, N70, `readmeImage` and ADR-009 d.8, the `package/versions` flag, transport/proxy/health in the root, the harness seam),
whether it needs a contract change behind the sentinel, and whether to split it. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: Split P4.9 into two tracker rows, P4.9a and P4.9b, both approved here; P4.9a is a contract-change item for one frozen file, `docs/adr/009-catalog.md`, sentinel content `P4.9a`. The shape: (e-i) one `FeedClients` object built by `createFeedClients(...)` in `src/core/catalog/feedClients.ts` plus a `FeedContexts` registry (`src/core/catalog/feedContexts.ts`) keyed by the effective `nuget.config` chain, both handed to the Catalog; (a-i) sharpened: project-scoped reads reach their chain through `ProjectContextProvider.get`, project-less reads take a `directory` argument from the host (`sourceDirectory(services)`), no protocol change; (b) `package/versions` and `package/metadata` for `'all'` are fan-outs over per-source coordinator resources (`resourceKeys.versions(id, source.url, pre)`, `resourceKeys.metadata(id, v, source.url)`), merged in the Catalog, the `'all'` keys never written (N70 closes); (c-i) `Catalog.readmeImage` lands in P4.9a together with the ADR-009 amendment under the sentinel; (d) `package/versions` with no versions and `sourcesUnavailable` is a `failed` error envelope, mapped in the handler; an incomplete answer (`sourcesUnavailable`, `offline`, or no metadata) is delivered but never cached, by rejecting the compute with a carrier error that `queryWithRetry` unwraps with its generation; (f) the root's `ActivationOverrides` gains `transport?: Transport` and the harness passes a scripted `FakeTransport`; (g) of the P2.8 list, `sourceHealth()` and `IconResolver.reset()` in `invalidate` return, `resetSourceHealth` is folded into `invalidate` (ADR-009 d.6), `resolvedSources` is not re-added (no request maps to it), enrichment of `installed/get` is deferred to P6.2 with the provisional chunk, and the installed views ask `transitive/metadata` meanwhile; `allProjects/installed` gets its `metadata` chunks in P4.9b. Nothing here is `OWNER MUST DECIDE`.

WHY: The brief describes the tree accurately: the nine Catalog gates (`src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts:189,197,251,283,287,291,295,299,308`), the five in `src/host/handlers.ts` (`:303,304,309,317,385`), `src/host/SidebarHost.ts:110`, the root's three (`src/extension.next.ts:72,205,274`), `CatalogDeps` without a feed member (`Catalog.ts:32-43`), every client of P4.3-P4.8 exported from `src/core/feeds/index.ts`, `NodeTransport` with `ProxyState` and `reset()` (`src/core/http/Transport.ts:27-30,344-350`), and `DefaultCredentialProvider` wanting `lookupConfigCredential` (`src/core/credentials/DefaultCredentialProvider.ts:19-22`). Five facts decide the design. (1) The coordinator never caches a rejected computation (`src/core/queries/QueryCoordinator.ts:321-348`: only `outcome.ok` reaches `store`; the error clears `entry.current` and rejects every attached handle), and it has no TTL (a value lives until `invalidate` or eviction), so "delivered but not cached" is a rejection that carries the value, unwrapped by the Catalog with the handle's still-valid `generation`; the alternative, invalidating after the fact, would list a bumped generation in `resources/invalidated` and make the webview drop the very response the host just sent (ADR-008). (2) `scopeMatchesKey` reaches `versions:<id>|<anything>` and `metadata:<id>@<anything>` by the id alone and every `versions:`/`metadata:` key by kind for `sources` (`src/core/queries/scopes.ts:51-62`), and a source's answer does not depend on the project: one coordinator query per allowed source makes the cache correct across projects by construction, which is the "explicit `sourceUrl`" option of the P4.8 ruling realised inside the Catalog, with no frozen key change and no invalidation from inside a read. (3) Chunks precede the terminal response (ADR-007, `src/protocol/envelope.ts`) and `installed/get` has no provisional chunk until P6.2 (ADR-009 d.3), so enriching inside `computeInstalled` would hold the first thing either surface can render until every icon is fetched; `transitive/metadata` takes `{ packages }` and answers `PackageMetadataLite[]` (`src/protocol/messages.ts:124`), which is the two-phase shape 1.x used, and the webview slices already keep lite metadata in a map keyed by lower-cased id (`src/webview/shared/store/installed.tsx:38-62`, `allProjects.tsx:66-70`). (4) The service-index client owns the health tracker and the endpoint cache (`src/core/feeds/serviceIndex.ts:150-170`), the monitor probes through one client (`src/core/feeds/health.ts:90-176`) and `sources/health` is one event for both surfaces, so that client and the credential provider it needs are shared; the provider caches a "none" answer for five minutes (`DefaultCredentialProvider.ts:108`), so any probe of a directory's sources must run after that directory's chain is registered, or a private feed answers 401 at every start. (5) `updates:<p>|pre` is a coordinator resource, and P2.fix-2 (C-protocol-host-7, enforced by `src/host/handlers.test.ts:213-231`) requires every cacheable read to report its generation, so `updates/get` carries one and the carrier must be unwrapped where the generation is known. ADR-005 ("effective `nuget.config` chain", `sourceUrls`, per project directory) and ADR-009 d.4/d.5 (host names the directory; sources, policy and credentials from the read's context) are met by keying the feed context on the chain and reaching it from `ProjectContextProvider.get(projectPath)` or from `configFilesFor(directory)`. The split follows plan §2.1 (one item ≤ a session-day; P4.9 spans three directories, the harness and an ADR; the P2 items of that size took 61 and 74 minutes each) and the tracker's `P1.fix-1`/`P2.fix-2` precedent for extra rows; the seam leaves every commit green with `tsc` 0 and no optional `feeds` dep (an optional member the root leaves undefined is the stub the P4.4 ruling refused).

Shared members: `transport`, `serviceIndex`, `credentials`, `flat = new DefaultFlatContainerClient({ transport, logger })`, `vulnerabilities = new DefaultVulnerabilityClient({ transport, logger })`, `readme = new ReadmeExtractor(transport, flat, { logger })`, `readmeImages = new ReadmeImageFetcher(transport, { getAuthHeader: url => credentials.getAuthHeader(url), logger })`, `offline = new OfflineMetadataReader({ globalPackagesFolder, logger })`, `iconCache = new TieredCacheIconCache(cache)`. `forPolicy(policy: OutboundPolicy): PolicyClients` builds one set per chain: `search = new DefaultSearchClient({ transport, runner, policy, logger })`, `registration = new DefaultRegistrationClient({ transport, policy, logger }, search, flat)`, `updates = new DefaultUpdateChecker({ policy, logger }, registration)`, `icons = new DefaultIconResolver(flat, iconCache, policy)`, `resolver = new DefaultMetadataResolver({ policy, logger }, { registration, flat, search, readme, offline })`, and two enrichers over the same `icons` and the same lite-cached lookup: `enricher = new DefaultMetadataEnricher({ policy, logger }, { lookup }, icons, vulnerabilities)` (live, for installed rows) and `searchEnricher = new DefaultMetadataEnricher({ policy, logger }, { lookup }, icons, NO_VULNERABILITY_DATA)` (for `search` and `updates`, so neither downloads the vulnerability index). `lookup = liteLookup(search)` is the `lite` cache's user: `(source, id, signal) => cache.get(cacheKeys.lite(id, source.source.url))` → a `PackageMetadataLite` or `null` (the source does not know the id) is answered without a request; a miss asks `search.lookup` and stores the answer or `null` under the `lite` kind; nothing else is stored (no icon, no vulnerabilities: icons have their own kind, vulnerabilities their own client cache). `NO_VULNERABILITY_DATA: VulnerabilityClient = { forPackage: async () => ({ vulnerabilities: [], sourcesUnavailable: true }), clear() {} }` ("not consulted": the enricher leaves `vulnerabilities` absent). `reset()`: `serviceIndex.clearCaches()`, `credentials.clear()`, `vulnerabilities.clear()`, `readmeImages.clear()`.

5. `src/core/catalog/feedContexts.ts` (new): `export class FeedContexts` with deps `{ contexts: Pick<ProjectContextProvider, 'get' | 'configFilesFor'>; sources: SourceProvider; configs: Pick<NuGetConfigReader, 'readChain'>; feeds: FeedClients; logger?: Logger }`. `export interface FeedContext { key: string; directory: string; configFiles: string[]; sources: NuGetSource[]; merged: MergedNuGetConfig; policy: OutboundPolicy; clients: PolicyClients }`. Two caches, both cleared by `clear()`: `directory → Promise<string[]>` (the chain of a directory) and `chain → Promise<FeedContext>`. `forDirectory(directory)`: the directory cache, filled from `contexts.configFilesFor(directory)` on a miss (never run `dotnet nuget config paths` per request), then `forChain(directory, configFiles)`. `forProject(projectPath)`: `directory = path.dirname(projectPath)`; on a directory-cache hit `forChain` at once; on a miss `(await contexts.get(projectPath)).context.configFiles` fills the directory cache (`ProjectContextProvider.get` has no cache of its own and `updates` recomputes after every operation); a rejection propagates and the caller decides. `forChain(directory, configFiles)`: key `configFiles.join('\n')` (the empty chain is the key `''`: no mapping, no config credentials, the listed sources; one `debug` line); on a miss `sources = await deps.sources.listSources(directory)`, `merged = mergeConfigChain(await configs.readChain(configFiles))`, `policy = new DefaultOutboundPolicy(merged.mapping)`, `clients = feeds.forPolicy(policy)`; a rejected build is deleted from the cache. `lookupConfigCredential(sourceUrl)`: over the settled contexts in insertion order, `credentialForUrl(sourceUrl, ctx.sources, ctx.merged)` (from `../credentials`), first hit, else `undefined`. `resolve(ctx, sourceUrls?: string[]): Promise<{ selected: NuGetSource[]; resolved: ResolvedSource[]; excluded: NuGetSource[] }>`: `selected = ctx.sources.filter(s => s.enabled && (sourceUrls === undefined || sourceUrls.includes(s.url)))`, `resolved = await feeds.serviceIndex.resolve(selected)`, `excluded` = the remote members of `selected` that `resolved` lacks (unhealthy or no usable endpoint). `clear()`: `icons.reset()` on every settled context's clients, then both caches emptied. Header comment states the invariant: a `getAuthHeader` for a source of directory D is asked only after `forDirectory(D)` or `forProject` settled (the provider caches "none" for five minutes). Deviation to record: the credential provider is shared and runs with its default `cwd` (home), not `context.projectDir` as the P2.7 recipe sketched; two chains that give the same URL different credentials share the 30-minute cache (first chain wins).

[sourceUrl] : undefined)`; `allowed = filterAllowedSources(ctx.policy, packageId, resolved)`; per allowed source `queryWithRetry` under `resourceKeys.versions(packageId, source.source.url, includePrerelease)` computing `ctx.clients.resolver.versions([source], packageId, { includePrerelease, listedOnly: false, signal })` (the explicit list includes unlisted versions, as the gotcha requires; update candidates stay listed-only in the checker), a `sourcesUnavailable` answer thrown as the carrier; merge: union, dedupe by `(normalize(v) ?? v).toLowerCase()` keeping the first text, `sortDescending`; `sourcesUnavailable = any source unavailable || excluded.length > 0` (one unhealthy source with no other allowed source must not read as a known empty list). A refused source is neither asked nor read; never build `resourceKeys.versions(id, undefined, …)`.
   - `metadata(directory, packageId, version, sourceUrl | undefined, signal) → Promise<PackageMetadata | undefined>`: allowed sources as above; in source order, `queryWithRetry` under `resourceKeys.metadata(packageId, version, source.source.url)` computing `ctx.clients.resolver.metadata([source], packageId, version, signal)`; an answer that is `undefined` or has `offline === true` means "not from this source" and is thrown as the carrier (the coordinator has no TTL: only a non-offline `PackageMetadata` may be cached); the first cached-able answer wins and stops the walk; when none answered, `ctx.clients.resolver.metadata([], packageId, version)` for the offline copy, outside the coordinator. Then `v = await feeds.vulnerabilities.forPackage(resolved, packageId, version, signal)`: set `vulnerabilities` unless `v.sourcesUnavailable` (absent = unknown), on the returned object only.

- Do not keep `CatalogDeps.feeds` optional, keep `NotYetAvailableError`, or leave any `REMOVAL GATE: P4.9` comment after P4.9b.
- Do not build `resourceKeys.versions(id, undefined, …)` or `resourceKeys.metadata(id, v, undefined)`; the `'all'` keys are reserved.
- Do not return a result with `sourcesUnavailable`, an `offline` metadata or `undefined` metadata from a compute function, and do not call `coordinator.invalidate` from inside a read to "uncache" it.
- Do not catch `IncompleteResultError` anywhere but in `queryWithRetry`; the generation travels with the value.
- Do not enrich inside `computeInstalled` or delay the `installed/get` response on the network; the provisional chunk is P6.2's.
- Do not ask `getAuthHeader` or `probe` for a directory's sources before `forDirectory`/`forProject` has registered its chain; the provider remembers "none" for five minutes.
- Do not add `projectPath` to any payload, a `ProtocolErrorCode`, a chunk kind or an `EventMap` member; `src/protocol/**` and `src/core/contracts.ts` stay byte-identical.
- Do not resolve sources, policy or credentials from a workspace-wide default; every read names a project or a directory the host chose (`sourceDirectory`).
- Do not run `dotnet nuget config paths` per request or per `forProject` call; the directory → chain cache is consulted first and cleared only in `invalidate`.
- Do not construct a second `DefaultServiceIndexClient`, `SourceHealthTracker` or `DefaultCredentialProvider`, or two `PolicyClients` sets per chain; only the enricher's vulnerability client differs.
- Do not hand the enricher of `search` or `updates` the live vulnerability client; the index download belongs to installed rows.
- Do not store icons or vulnerabilities in a `lite` entry; only the lookup answer.
- Do not emit a `health` chunk on `sources/list`, and do not invalidate anything from a health pass.
- Do not probe every project directory from the monitor; the selected directory and the first workspace folder, through registered chains.
- Do not pass an `agent`, `rejectUnauthorized`, `undici` or `fetch` to the transport; the predicate is the P4.1 text, evaluated per call.
- Do not test for `nuget.org` anywhere in `src/core/catalog/*.ts` outside tests.
- Do not add a search cache, a `resolvedSources` method or a `resetSourceHealth` method.
- Do not import from `src/core/feeds/testSupport.ts` outside test files, and do not export it from the barrel.
- Do not assert "exactly one feed request" or "exactly one `sources/health` event" in the scenarios; the lookups and the reset make both false.
- Do not create the sentinel before this answer is pasted and the tracker rows exist; do not commit while it exists; the sentinel is `P4.9a` only.
- Do not start P4.9b before P4.9a's CI run is green.

### P4.9b — stop-and-ask: how the health monitor obtains its chains (2026-10-16)

Brief: with the monitor of the P4.9 ruling's step 12 in place, six harness scenarios failed because the probe walked
`dotnet nuget config paths` a second time per directory; with the probe disabled all 16 passed. Addendum: two all-projects
Catalog tests now see the step-14 `metadata` chunk. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: Option 2, sharpened, with option 1's probe mechanism folded in. The chain of a project directory is registered by the `installed` computation's own walk (`Catalog.computeInstalled` hands the `configFiles` of the `ProjectContextProvider.get` it already runs to a new `FeedContexts.register`); `computeUpdates` asks `installed` before `forProject`; the health monitor walks no directory and reads no session: it probes the enabled sources of the chains already registered (`FeedContexts.registered()`) and is restarted by a new `FeedContexts.onDidRegister` event. The `reconciled`/`markReconciled` gate added for observation (1) is removed. No existing harness scenario changes; of my P4.9 ruling, step 12's probe recipe is replaced (not patched), step 15's "recorded during activation, before either surface exists" premise is withdrawn and the two P4.9b scenarios/root tests are reworded below. Addendum: the two Catalog tests `allProjectsInstalled streams protocol chunks` and `allProjectsInstalled sends a second chunk when an evaluation delivers the authoritative result` are rewritten by title to expect the `metadata` chunk; the rig default stays. Nothing here is `OWNER MUST DECIDE`.

WHY: The brief is accurate about the tree, with two additions it did not list: `src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts` already carries step 14 (`emitInstalledMetadata`, uncommitted diff), and `src/test/harness/harness.ts` plus an untracked `src/test/harness/fakeFeed.ts` already pass `transport: new FakeTransport(feed.handler)` (step 15's seam; `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` shows both). The defect is not in the monitor but in a duplicated walk: `Catalog.computeInstalled` runs `this.deps.contexts.get(projectPath)` (`src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts:178`), which is the one `dotnet nuget config paths` of a directory (`src/core/project/context.ts:39-43,73-85`), and discards the chain; `FeedContexts.forDirectory` (`src/core/catalog/feedContexts.ts:58-65`) and `forProject` (`:68-82`) then walk the same directory again, which is what the probe (`src/extension.next.ts:222-237`), `computeUpdates` (`Catalog.ts:220` before `installed` at `:229`: two walks for a fresh `updates/get`) and step 14 (`Catalog.ts` diff, `forProject` in `emitInstalledMetadata`) each do. The harness pins the single walk on purpose (`src/test/harness/scenarios.test.ts:116,207,244,269,282`, gotcha "Harness: a read that cannot be held"), so any design that adds a `nuget config paths` for a project directory outside its `installed` computation breaks it, and options 4 and 5 would only hide that from the suite that counts it. My step 12 sentence "the probe reuses the cached listing of the same directory and must add none" was true of `nuget list source` (`DotnetSourceProvider.listings`, `src/core/sources/DotnetSourceProvider.ts:45-59`) and wrong about the chain; the recipe built on it is withdrawn. Registering from the computation keeps ADR-002 invariant 1 and ADR-009 d.5 ("a source is probed or warmed only after the chain of its directory is registered") literally true, costs no new process (`register` reuses the cached listing and reads a chain already known), and leaves every frozen file untouched. Probing the union of registered chains also serves `ALL_PROJECTS` (every project's chain is registered by the fan-out) and project-less reads (a `search` registers the host's directory via `forDirectory`), which the selected-directory recipe did not. One accepted residual: a `sources` invalidation clears the chains (`Catalog.ts:533-539`) without bumping `installed:` keys (ADR-002 scope table), so the next feed read of a cached project walks once through `forProject`'s miss; no scenario holds at that moment, and after a `nuget.config` change a fresh walk is right.

Add `registered(): readonly FeedContext[]` (`[...this.settled.values()]`) and `readonly onDidRegister: Event<FeedContext>` (an `Emitter` from `../util/events`), fired in `forChain`'s success branch right after `this.settled.set(key, built)`, so a context reached by `register`, `forProject` or `forDirectory` fires once per chain, again after `clear()` rebuilds it. ### P5.5 — stop-and-ask: the sidebar's skeleton-count tests and the Updates section (2026-10-16)

Brief: with the sidebar Updates section mounted, four tests of `SidebarView.test.tsx` that the item did not write failed at
document-wide `.nuiget-skeleton-row` counts (the section shows its own loading skeleton); options were re-scoping the
queries, no skeleton, a collapsed section, or answering `updates/get` in those tests. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: Option 1. Re-scope the six skeleton-row queries of `src/webview/sidebar-next/SidebarView.test.tsx` (lines 62, 65, 71, 260, 277, 290) to the Installed section's content; every other assertion of the four tests stays byte-for-byte. The four tests that may change, by title: `shows skeleton rows while the first list is loading, then the packages of the selected project`; `revalidate without blanking: the rows stay, the list is busy and a progress bar shows until the new list is there`; `another project: its packages replace the list after skeleton rows, never mixed`; `an error is a banner with Retry; a list that is shown stays under it`. No other test of that file changes. The Updates section keeps its `<Skeleton density="compact" />`, starts expanded, and gets its own test file.

WHY: The brief is right about the tree: `UpdatesSection.tsx:70-75` renders a `Skeleton` while `session === undefined` and while the first `updates/get` is pending, and `Skeleton.tsx:17` emits 3 `.nuiget-skeleton-row` divs, so at `SidebarView.test.tsx:62` (before `session/get` is answered) the document holds 6 rows, and at :65/:260/:290 it holds 3 where 0 or 3 was asserted. ### P5.6 — stop-and-ask: the source list of quick-search and `searchDebounceMode` (2026-10-15)

Brief: `search/autocomplete` takes `sources: Array<{ name; url }>` and resolves nothing for `[]`, so under the default
`'all'` the webview must enumerate the enabled sources; no 2.0 webview asks `sources/list`, and the `sources` slice was
assigned to P5.8; `searchDebounceMode` comes from `config/get`/`config/changed` and no slice owns config. Options were a
private read in the search slice, the read part of the `sources` slice landing here, quick-search deferred to P5.8, or
quick-search only for a single selected source. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: Option 2, narrowed: the read part of the `sources` slice (`src/webview/shared/store/sources.tsx` + test) and a small `config` slice (`store/config.tsx` + test) land in P5.6, mounted in `StoreProvider`, both asking only after a consumer calls `enable()`; the `search` slice owns the `search/autocomplete` request; the main search feature owns the timers; P5.8 adds the source mutations and enables the selector. N57 (`full`/`off`) stays with P5.13.

Tree correction first: the brief says "No edits yet", but at c4c3617 the working tree already has `src/webview/shared/store/search.tsx` (175 lines, `SearchProvider` over `committed.selectedSource` and `includePrerelease`, `metadata` chunk merged, latest text wins) and `search.test.tsx` (9 titles) untracked, `StoreProvider.tsx` mounting `SearchProvider` inside `AllProjectsProvider`, and `src/core/feeds/enricher.ts`, `enricher.test.ts`, `src/host/handlers.test.ts` and `docs/plans/STATUS.md` modified. All of it is inside the P5.6 row's text (the slice, "bind the enrichment to the request signal", the `handlers.test.ts` title from the P4 review), so nothing there is a stop-and-ask; this ruling takes that WIP as given.

WHY: The P3.6 ruling's rule is "each slice lands with its first consumer" (`docs/plans/STATUS.md:81`); its `sources → P5.8` entry was a forecast of who that consumer would be. `search/autocomplete` is the first 2.0 consumer of `sources/list`: its frozen payload (`src/protocol/messages.ts:133`) carries `sources: Array<{ name; url }>`, the host maps only the URLs (`src/host/handlers.ts:301`), `Catalog.quickSearch` hands them to `FeedContexts.resolve` whose filter `sourceUrls === undefined || sourceUrls.includes(source.url)` (`src/core/catalog/feedContexts.ts:115`) resolves nothing for `[]`, and `Catalog.ts:439` then answers `[]`, so under the default `'all'` the webview must enumerate enabled sources itself, as 1.x did from `enabledSourcesRef` (`src/webview/app/App.tsx:1882-1887`). Option 1 writes a second subscriber to `sources` invalidation that P5.8 deletes (work lost, which the advisor's tiebreak forbids); option 3 removes "quick-search" from a row that names it (plan line 279) and §2's "(quick-search suggestions while typing)"; option 4 ships no quick-search under the default setting. `search/query` needs no list (`sourceUrls?: string[]`, `undefined` = every enabled source, `messages.ts:132`, `feedContexts.ts:115`), and the sidebar's browse is "Enter or 300 ms debounce, min 2 chars" with no suggestions (`docs/ux/interaction-model.md:26`), so only the main panel's quick-search reads the list and `searchDebounceMode`; a lazy `enable()` (the `transitive` precedent, `store/transitive.tsx:20-21`) keeps `StoreProvider.test.tsx:33-35` R1 ("on start it asks session/get and projects/list, and nothing else") and ARCHITECTURE.md:377-378 literally true and leaves the sidebar's request set unchanged. `searchDebounceMode` is `ExtensionConfig` (`src/protocol/domain.ts:330`), read by `config/get` (`messages.ts:113`) and pushed to both surfaces as `config/changed` (`src/host/MainPanelHost.ts:87`, `src/host/SidebarHost.ts:39`); other fields (`treeIndent`, `isWindows`, `enablePerformanceLogging`) have later consumers, so a slice is right, and `config` not being in ADR-008's enumeration (`docs/adr/008-webview-architecture.md:25-27`) is recorded as a deviation, not an ADR edit (D6; the P5.2 sweep's gate "ADR-008's slice list ⊆ store" holds with one more). The host maps the contributed `full` and `off` (`package.json:259-263`) to `quicksearch` (`src/host/services.ts:93`); that is finding N57 (`docs/plans/findings-ledger.md:160,403`), owned by "the P5 item that ports the search settings" with a `contributes` ⚑ and a `domain.ts` sentinel if the type changes, which is P5.13's row (plan line 286), not P5.6.

DO:
1. `src/webview/shared/store/sources.tsx` (+ `sources.test.tsx`): `SourcesProvider`/`useSources()` → `{ sources: readonly NuGetSource[] | undefined; failed: readonly FailedSource[]; status; error; revalidating; enable(); refresh() }`. `enable()` is idempotent and sticky for the surface (JSDoc says so: unlike `transitive.enable()` it does not reset per project). Once enabled and `useSession().committed` is defined, request `sources/list` (empty payload; the host answers for the committed project's directory, `handlers.ts:29-35`); ask again when `committed.selectedProject` changes, on `refresh()`, and on a `resources/invalidated` event with `scope.kind === 'sources'` or any `keys[].key` starting with `sources:`. Not a `useResource` (the key is `sources:<projectDir>` and the webview may not take `dirname`); mirror `allProjects.tsx:106-107`: latest request wins (abort the earlier one), keep the shown list until the answer. `failed` comes from the answer, from the `health` chunk, and from `sources/health` events. Tests (titles): `asks nothing until it is enabled, then sources/list once`; `a committed project change asks again and keeps the list while it does`; `an invalidation of scope sources or a sources: key asks again, and the latest answer wins`; `failed follows the answer, the health chunk and sources/health`; `an error ends loading and refresh asks again`.
2. `src/webview/shared/store/config.tsx` (+ `config.test.tsx`): `ConfigProvider`/`useConfig()` → `{ config: ExtensionConfig | undefined; enable() }`. `config/changed` events always apply; `enable()` asks `config/get` once if nothing is known yet. Tests: `asks nothing until it is enabled, then config/get once`; `config/changed replaces the value, also before enable`.
3. `StoreProvider.tsx`: mount `ConfigProvider` and `SourcesProvider` (inside `SessionProvider`, next to the already-added `SearchProvider`). `StoreProvider.test.tsx` R1 stays as it is and must stay green; its StrictMode test too.
4. `store/search.tsx` (the WIP): add quick-search ownership: `suggest(query)`, `suggestions: readonly QuickSearchSourceResult[]`, `suggesting: boolean`, `clearSuggestions()`. `suggest` reads `useSources().sources`, `useConfig().config` and the committed session; it sends `search/autocomplete` with `includePrerelease` from the committed session and `sources` = enabled sources mapped to `{ name, url }` when `selectedSource === 'all'`, else the enabled source whose `url === selectedSource`; when the list is unknown or the mapping is empty it sends nothing and clears suggestions. Latest wins: abort the earlier request. Add to `search.test.tsx`: `suggest asks search/autocomplete with every enabled source under all and the one selected source otherwise`; `suggest sends nothing while the sources are unknown or none matches`; `a newer suggest cancels the earlier request and its answer never shows`.
5. Main search feature (`src/webview/main/features/search/`, this row's): a hook that calls `sources.enable()` and `config.enable()` in a mount effect (not on the first keystroke: a 150 ms timer would beat the list back). While `config` is undefined, nothing runs while typing. `'quicksearch'`: 150 ms after ≥ 2 characters in browse mode, text not starting with `@`, input focused → `suggest(text)`; `'fullsearch'`: 300 ms → `search(text)`, no suggestions. Enter always runs `search(text)` at once and cancels the pending timer and suggestions; Escape and a mode change clear suggestions. `ui/navigateToPackage` → fill the box, `search(id, { exactMatch: true })`. Test both modes through `config/get` answers (and one `config/changed` switch), the `@` gating, and `Enter cancels the pending debounce`.
6. Sidebar browse (`SidebarView.tsx`, this row's by the P5.5 ruling): Enter or 300 ms debounce with ≥ 2 characters → `search(text)`; it reads neither `useSources` nor `useConfig` and never calls `enable()`.
7. Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md store list gets `config` (P5.6, "not in ADR-008's enumeration, lazy") and `sources` ("read part P5.6, lazy `enable()`, mutations P5.8") bullets and the sentence at :377-378 unchanged; `src/webview/shared/STATUS.md` records the `config` slice as a deviation from ADR-008:25-27 and the N57 behaviour (`full`/`off` arrive as `quicksearch`); `docs/plans/findings-ledger.md` N57 owner column → P5.13; tracker row P5.8 note: "the read part of `sources` landed in P5.6 (first consumer, P3.6); this row adds the mutations and enables `source-selector`"; row P5.2's assignment line amended the same way; paste this ruling verbatim under "Advisor decisions".

DO NOT:
Send `search/autocomplete` with `sources: []`, or before the list is known (the host answers `[]`; show no suggestions instead).
Enable or populate `source-selector` in `MainShell.tsx`; that is P5.8's by the P5.3 STATUS note (`src/webview/main/STATUS.md:176-178`).
Add an `'off'` branch, map `'full'` in the webview, touch `src/host/services.ts:93`, `package.json` `contributes`, or `ExtensionConfig` (N57 → P5.13, ⚑).
Rewrite `StoreProvider.test.tsx` R1 or ARCHITECTURE.md:377-378 to admit a start-up `sources/list` or `config/get`.
Put a quick-search timer, a private source list or a `config/get` in the sidebar or in any feature; the feature owns timers only and asks the slice.
Use `useResource` for sources with a key built from `dirname(selectedProject)`.
Call `enable()` on the first keystroke instead of on mount.
Edit `docs/adr/008-webview-architecture.md` to add `config` (frozen, D6; record the deviation instead).

CONTRACT CHANGE: none. `src/protocol/**`, `src/core/contracts.ts` and `docs/adr/**` stay untouched; `search/autocomplete`'s payload is used as frozen. The N57 fix (contributes enum and, if the type widens, `domain.ts:330` under a sentinel) belongs to P5.13, which is ⚑ mandatory.

### P5.6 — stop-and-ask: the main entry's start requests (2026-10-15)

Brief: following ruling 1, the main search feature enables the `config` and `sources` slices on mount, so the main
entry now also asks `config/get` at start, and `src/webview/main/index.test.tsx`'s first test (P5.3), which asserts
exactly `session/get` and `projects/list`, failed; options were rewriting it by title, enabling on the box's first
focus, or deferring `config/get` behind the session. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: Option 1. Rewrite `src/webview/main/index.test.tsx:35` (and its title, line 20) to expect exactly `session/get`, `projects/list` and `config/get` from the main entry; the test is named here by title, so P5.6 may rewrite it. `useSearchTyping.ts:47-50` (enable on mount) stays as it is; `StoreProvider.test.tsx` R1, `src/webview/sidebar-next/index.test.tsx` and ARCHITECTURE.md:377-378 stay byte-for-byte.

WHY: The brief is right about the tree: `config.tsx:28-36` asks `config/get` as soon as `enabled` is set and nothing else is known (no session needed, as its JSDoc at `config.tsx:9` says), `sources.tsx:50,66-84` asks `sources/list` only once `enabled && committed !== undefined`, and `useSearchTyping.ts:47-50` enables both in a mount effect, so the main entry's first burst is `session/get`, `projects/list`, `config/get`, and `index.test.tsx:35` (which counts every `kind === 'request'` envelope during `import('./index')`) must fail by one member while the sidebar entry (which enables neither, DO 6; `grep useSources\|useConfig src/webview/sidebar-next` → 0) is unchanged. The gap is in my ruling of 2026-10-15, not in the item: DO 5 required the mount-time `enable()` and the DO NOT line protected two claims that stay literally true (R1 "the store alone asks nothing else", `StoreProvider.test.tsx:31-35`; ARCHITECTURE.md:377-378 "the other slices ask when they have something to ask for"), but it did not look at the two entry tests, which assert a different claim: what a *surface* asks when it opens. Changing that assertion to the exact new set keeps its count-and-meaning shape ("acquire once, mount, and nothing beyond these start requests"), which is the re-scoping the P5.5 ruling allowed for `SidebarView.test.tsx`, not a weakening under RUN.md:82; `index.tsx` is an item file (the item edits it to pass `browse=`), so its test is in scope by plan §2.1, and P5.3/P5.4 set the precedent of rewriting `index.test.tsx` in place (`docs/plans/STATUS.md:589`, `src/webview/main/STATUS.md:129,166`). Option 2 is the move my DO NOT "Call `enable()` on the first keystroke instead of on mount" forbids with a weaker trigger: a focus-then-type burst (also the host's `ui/focusSearch`, `MainShell.tsx:78`) would start the 150 ms timer before `config` or the list is back, and it changes product behaviour to dodge a test (rejected for the same reason in the P5.5 ruling). Option 3 gives the config slice a session dependency its contract does not have and passes only because the entry test never answers `session/get`; the next test that does would fail the same way.

DO:
1. `src/webview/main/index.test.tsx`: title at :20 → `mounts the shell into its root, acquires the API once and asks the host for the session, the projects and the settings`; assertion at :35 → `expect(new Set(asked)).toEqual(new Set(['session/get', 'projects/list', 'config/get']));`. Add one comment line above it: `// The search feature enables the config and sources slices on mount: config needs no session; sources/list follows the first snapshot (useSearchTyping.test.tsx, sources.test.tsx).` Nothing else in the file changes: `new Set(asked)` already absorbs StrictMode's second `config/get`, and the abort of the first one posts `kind: 'cancel'` (`MessageBus.ts:110-114`), which the `kind === 'request'` filter at :34 drops.
2. Do not extend the entry test to answer `session/get` and assert `sources/list`: the entry's bus listens on the `window` default, and answering there means dispatching a `MessageEvent` by hand, which the gotcha reserves for `MessageBus.test.ts`. The order (config at once, sources after the snapshot, both before any key) is already asserted by `useSearchTyping.test.tsx:56-60` (`enables the settings and the source list when the panel opens, before any key`, which answers the session first at :32) and by `sources.test.tsx` (`asks nothing until it is enabled, then sources/list once`); cite both in the STATUS note.

### P5.8 — stop-and-ask: the config chain for `configFile` attribution in `Catalog.sources()` (2026-10-15)

Brief: the P5.8 row asks for `configFile` attribution of `sources()` with `withConfigFiles`; the merged config of a
directory exists only on a `FeedContext`, `forDirectory` walks `dotnet nuget config paths` for an unregistered
directory, the main panel asks `sources/list` on mount since P5.6, every source mutation clears the contexts, and the
harness holds count `nuget config paths` walks. Options were attribution through `forDirectory` inside `sources()`, a
settled context only, the project context's chain, or no attribution. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: A refined option 1, call it 1b: `Catalog.sources(projectDir, signal?, options?: { configFiles?: boolean })` attributes at read time, outside the cached compute, through `feedContexts.forDirectory(dir)` and only when the caller asks for it; the `sources/list`, `sources/refresh` and the four mutation handlers ask, the root's reconcile and the sidebar picker do not; and `computeInstalled` announces its own walk to `FeedContexts` before awaiting it, so a concurrent `forDirectory`/`forProject` joins that walk instead of spawning a second `dotnet nuget config paths`. Not options 2, 3 or 4.

WHY: Two corrections to the brief first. (i) The tree is further along than "only the tracker row edited": `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` shows `src/webview/main/MainShell.tsx`, `main.css`, `src/webview/shared/store/sources.tsx` and `sources.test.tsx` modified and `src/webview/main/features/sources/{SourceSettingsDialog,SourcesControl,SourcesControl.test}.tsx` plus `src/test/ui/v2/main-sources.ui.test.ts` untracked, all P5.8's webview side; `SourceSettingsDialog.tsx:34,46` already passes `source.configFile` to `remove` and shows it, so the attribution is load-bearing, not optional. (ii) Option 3's premise is false: `ProjectContextProvider` has no cache (`src/core/project/context.ts:37-43` runs `configFilesFor` on every `get`; the per-directory cache the gotcha mentions is the runner's SDK probe), and `sources()` has a directory, not a project path. The deciding facts: ADR-009 d.5 names exactly this path for a read without a project ("through the directory the host names"), and every other directory-scoped read already takes it (`Catalog.ts:271,415,437,504,516,532`), so attribution through `forDirectory` is the ADR's shape, not a new one; but `sources()` is also on the activation and reconcile path (`src/extension.next.ts:149-191`, `enabledSourceUrls` inside `refreshProjectsAndSession`, awaited as `extension.ready` by `src/test/harness/harness.ts:173` and re-run on every `workspace`/`sources`/`project` invalidation at `:241-245`), so a walk inside the compute would spawn at activation and during every full refresh and turn `src/extension.next.test.ts:365` (no walk before a read) and `:373` (one after), `src/test/harness/scenarios.test.ts:270` (one walk per directory) and `:119/:125/:142` (`recomputation.seen` 1 then 2 under a held walk) red: six assertions in tests the item does not name, all encoding ADR-002's one-computation invariant. Option 2 cannot attribute after a mutation: the `sources` scope reaches `sources, updates:*, allProjects:updates*, versions:*, metadata:*` and never `installed:*` (`src/core/queries/scopes.ts:17`), so after `afterSourceMutation`'s `feedContexts.clear()` (`Catalog.ts:541-546`, `handlers.ts:336-341`) nothing re-registers a chain before the mutation's own `catalog.sources` answers, which is exactly the add-then-remove window the dialog exists for. Option 4 defers the P2.8 note a second time while the dialog consumes it. Attribution outside the compute keeps the cached `sources:<dir>` value the plain listing (so the root's activation read is a cache hit without a walk and `Catalog.test.ts:347` `sources queries per directory` is untouched), and the flag confines the walk to the five handlers, whose callers in the harness and the root test never send `sources/list` on their own (`grep` of `src/test/harness/*.ts` hits only `scenarios.test.ts:625`, which asks after `walk.release()` and `expectState`, when the chain is registered and `forDirectory` spawns nothing). The attributed value stays under the listing's generation: the chain is cleared by the same invalidations that clear the listing (`sources`, `workspace`; the nuget.config watcher at `extension.next.ts:311` fires `sources`), and a `project` invalidation clears neither. The pending-chain announcement in `FeedContexts` dedupes the mount walk in the order `installed/get` then `sources/list` without touching `context.ts` (P2.5's file) and keeps each hold's per-computation meaning (`register` today runs only after `contexts.get` resolved, `Catalog.ts:184-188`, which is why `forDirectory` finds nothing while the walk is in flight). The P4.9 DO NOT at `src/core/catalog/STATUS.md:562` ("not per request or per `forProject` call; the directory → chain cache is consulted first and cleared only in `invalidate`") is satisfied by the flagged path; the P2.8 DO NOT at `src/core/catalog/STATUS.md:458` ("Do not call `withConfigFiles` or run `dotnet nuget config paths` from `sources()`") is superseded for this item, by name.

DO:
1. `src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts`: change the signature to `sources(projectDir: string, signal?: AbortSignal, options: { configFiles?: boolean } = {}): Promise<CatalogValue<NuGetSource[]>>`. Keep the compute exactly as it is (`queryWithRetry` under `resourceKeys.sources(projectDir)` over `this.deps.sources.listSources(projectDir)`). After it resolves: if `!options.configFiles` return it unchanged; otherwise `const context = await this.deps.feedContexts.forDirectory(projectDir).catch((error: unknown) => { this.deps.logger?.warn(redact(`Config chain of ${projectDir} could not be read, sources unattributed: ${describe(error)}`)); return undefined; });` and return `{ value: context ? withConfigFiles(listed.value, context.merged) : listed.value, generation: listed.generation }`. Import `withConfigFiles` from `'../sources'` (exported at `src/core/sources/index.ts:17`). Use the compute's own listing, never `context.sources`: contexts are keyed by chain (`feedContexts.ts:132-136`), and two directories whose walk failed share the key `''` and the first directory's listing (`:155-159`).
2. `src/core/catalog/feedContexts.ts` (approved deviation, same directory, with `feedContexts.test.ts`): `register(projectPath: string, chain: string[] | Promise<string[]>): Promise<FeedContext>`. For a promise: `this.chains.set(directory, chain)`, then the same four lines as `forProject` (`:94-98`) deleting the entry on rejection when it is still the current one, then `return this.forChain(directory, await chain)`. An array keeps today's behaviour, so the existing test at `:135` (`register seeds a directory's chain …`) stays as it is.
3. `src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts` `computeInstalled` (`:175-188`): take the raw promise first, `const raw = this.deps.contexts.get(projectPath); void this.deps.feedContexts.register(projectPath, raw.then(result => result.context.configFiles)).catch(debug as today);` before the `Promise.all`, and attach the existing `.catch(warn → undefined)` to `raw` for the `Promise.all`. The chain must be derived from the uncaught promise: deriving it from the caught one would register the empty chain `''` for a failed source listing and cache it until the next `clear()`, losing `forProject`'s recovery. Delete the post-resolution `register` block at `:184-188`.
4. `src/host/handlers.ts`: `listSources` (`:319-322`) calls `catalog.sources(sourceDirectory(services), signal, { configFiles: true })`; `afterSourceMutation` (`:338`) calls `catalog.sources(sourceDirectory(services), undefined, { configFiles: true })`. The `removedUrl`/`disabledUrl` pre-reads (`:353,373`), `src/extension.next.ts:154` and `src/host/SidebarHost.ts:88` stay without the flag.
5. Tests, by title. `src/core/catalog/Catalog.test.ts` (build the rig once and pass `rig.sources` into `makeDeps` next to `rig.feedContexts`: the rig's `FeedContexts` lists through its own `fakeSources(listings)` at `:138-141`, and an override provider would make `build`'s call invisible): `sources with configFiles names the declaring file from the directory's chain and runs no config-paths command once the chain is registered` (seed through `installed(appPath)` with `documents` for the chain, then `sources(dir, undefined, { configFiles: true })` → the feed carries `configFile`, `contexts.configFilesFor` not called); `sources with configFiles walks a chain no computation registered once, and forProject then shares it` (`configFilesFor` called once across `sources(dir, …, { configFiles: true })` and a following `updates(appPath, …)`); `sources with configFiles answers the bare listing when the chain cannot be built` (`configs.readChain` rejects → the listing without `configFile`, generation unchanged, a warning logged); `sources without configFiles runs no config-paths command` (the activation path: `configFilesFor` never called). Leave `sources queries per directory` (`:347`) exactly as it is: it passes no flag. `src/core/catalog/feedContexts.test.ts`: `register with a pending walk is joined by forDirectory and forProject before it settles` (one `configFilesFor` call, both resolve to the same context); `a rejected pending registration leaves no chain and the next forDirectory walks`. `src/host/handlers.test.ts`: extend the per-request test so the five sources handlers (`sources/list`, `sources/refresh`, the four mutations' `afterSourceMutation`) are asserted to pass `{ configFiles: true }` and the two pre-reads not to.
6. Webview (already drafted): the remove confirm names `source.configFile` when present and sends `sources/remove { sourceName, configFile }` only then; a source without `configFile` is removed from the nearest file (the host's default) and the confirm says so. The ExTester test polls for the final list after a mutation: a mutation costs two walks (its own `sources` invalidation and the nuget.config watcher's about a second later), each re-ask walks once; never assert on the first refresh.
7. `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, row "A recovered source invalidates nothing": replace "`dotnet nuget config paths` for a project directory runs inside `ProjectContextProvider.get` only, and `computeInstalled` hands that chain to `FeedContexts.register` (the harness holds on it rely on that)" with: "`dotnet nuget config paths` for a project directory runs in `ProjectContextProvider.get`, whose pending walk `computeInstalled` registers with `FeedContexts` before awaiting it, and in `FeedContexts.forDirectory` only for a directory no computation has registered (any directory read, `sources(…, { configFiles: true })` included); the harness holds count walks, so a scenario that asks `sources/list` while a walk is held counts one more". Keep the row's remaining sentences.
8. Ledger: record N72, "mount-time double walk of `nuget config paths` when `sources/list` is dispatched before `installed/get` for the same directory (the pending-chain announcement covers the other order only)", pointed at P6.2, which rewrites `computeInstalled`'s context path. Cite P5.8, ADR-009 (d.5), N72 in the commit.
9. STATUS notes: `src/core/catalog/STATUS.md` (this ruling verbatim, the P2.8 DO NOT at `:458` marked superseded by P5.8, the `:312` "Not started" line closed), `src/host/STATUS.md`, the webview notes, `docs/plans/STATUS.md` row P5.8.
10. Gates in §2.2 order, including `npm run check-types`, `node esbuild.mjs --v2 --production --analyze` with the three sizes pasted (core and host changed), the harness matrix at `scenarios.test.ts:95` and the two source scenarios 40 times each. If part 2 (steps 2-3) moves any harness count, it is severable: drop steps 2-3, keep steps 1 and 4, and widen N72 to both orders; a red harness from part 2 is not a stop.

DO NOT:
Do not put `forDirectory` or `withConfigFiles` inside the compute function of `sources:<dir>`; the root's activation read would then walk, or (with a per-caller compute) cache an unattributed value that every later `sources/list` hits.
Do not attribute from `feedContexts.registered()` or any settled-only lookup; after a `sources` invalidation nothing re-registers before the mutation's answer (`scopes.ts:17`).
Do not pass the flag from `src/extension.next.ts:154`, `SidebarHost.ts:88` or the `removedUrl`/`disabledUrl` pre-reads.
Do not touch `src/core/project/context.ts` or give `ProjectContextProvider` a cache: the holds and `revision` need one walk per computation.
Do not derive the pending chain from the caught `contexts.get` promise (step 3).
Do not use `context.sources` as the listing; use the compute's listing.
Do not rewrite `sources queries per directory`, `extension.next.test.ts:357-374` or any harness count; if one moves, the implementation is wrong, not the test.
Do not add a Catalog method (`configFilesOf`, `sourceUrls`): ADR-009 d.8 and the sentinel.
Do not re-ask `sources/list` from the webview after `installed/get` as a workaround for N72, and do not `invalidate` from `onDidRegister`.
Do not fix here that a failed walk (`configFilesFor` → `[]`) is cached as chain `''` until the next `clear()` (pre-existing in P4.9a's `forDirectory`); `sources/refresh` is the user's way out.

CONTRACT CHANGE: none. `NuGetSource.configFile?` exists at `src/protocol/domain.ts:147`; `sources/remove { sourceName, configFile? }` at `src/protocol/messages.ts:148` is unchanged; no ADR amendment, no sentinel. `src/core/catalog/feedContexts.ts` and `feedContexts.test.ts` are approved as a named deviation from the row's file list (record it in both STATUS notes).

Same situation as the P5.4 brief, same remedy: ordered green commits, each pushed and green before the next. A second correction, from the brief itself and confirmed: `git ls-files src/test/e2e/fixtures` lists `TestProject.csproj` and `nuget.config`, so `src/test/ui/v2/STATUS.md` ("the fixture workspace has no `nuget.config`", also in the P5.8 deviation paragraph) and the comment at `src/test/ui/v2/main-sources.ui.test.ts:10` are wrong; fix both in this item's STATUS rewrite.

DECISION:
(1) `sdk-too-old`: no separate "Unsupported" group. Every unsupported project keeps its own section in its workspace folder, in the host's project order, with an `Unsupported` badge on its `SectionHeader` and the existing banner "Unsupported project: <message>" as the first content; an `sdk-too-old` project shows its package list under the banner, read-only; any other reason (`packages-config`, `non-sdk-style`, `parse-failed`, `not-found`) shows the banner alone, no `Listbox`, no `count`. The same rule applies in the single-project view, which `InstalledProjectSection` already serves.
(2) All Projects updates: option a. P5.9 owns the `allProjects/updates` stream (in the `allProjects` slice) and its consumer in `UpdatesTab`, as its own green commit; N11 closes here. The sidebar's two "All Projects is not available in this view yet" states are P5.10's and go on P5.10's row.
(3) ExTester: a fourth option, narrower than the three: the new `src/test/ui/v2/main-all-projects.ui.test.ts` creates a second SDK-style project inside the opened fixture workspace in `before`, waits for the host to offer "All Projects (2)", proves the grouping on the real host, and removes the project in `after`. No tracked fixture, no script, no CI job and no existing test changes. The harness scenarios remain the proof of the late-chunk rule; folder headings and `sdk-too-old` are proved in jsdom and the test's JSDoc and the STATUS note say why VS Code cannot show them on the runners.
(4) Line 166: option 1. Re-scope that one assertion of `InstalledTab.test.tsx:155` (`All Projects: one section per project, selections across them become ops/bulkRemoveAllProjects with the project names`) to "the aggregate `transitive-section` is present and collapsed, and neither `transitive/get` nor `allProjects/transitive` has been asked"; everything else in the test stays byte-for-byte.
Also decided, as the row asks: `touchedBy` keeps its flat record; the recorded deviation stays and the shape question goes to the P5 phase review.

WHY:
(1) `src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts:206-207` gives an `sdk-too-old` project its packages plus `unsupported` (D13: read-only, packages listed), while `src/core/project/inspector.ts:93-97` gives the other four reasons `unsupported` with no packages; both reach `allProjects/installed` as a `project` chunk (`Catalog.ts:319-321`). Interaction model §4 (`docs/ux/interaction-model.md:62`) says "Row/banner 'Unsupported project: <reason>' from `InstalledResult.unsupported`", which the section header plus `InstalledProjectSection.tsx:91`'s banner satisfies; §3 (`:36-39`) and D2 group by workspace folder only, so a separate Unsupported group would pull a project out of its folder and out of P5.4's option D (one `SectionHeader` and one list per project). Today an unsupported project without packages renders an empty list saying "No packages installed." (`InstalledProjectSection.tsx:53-55,93`), which is "empty is not unknown" in reverse. `whyNotRemovable` (`src/webview/shared/installed/rules.ts:26-27`) already makes every row of an unsupported project non-removable, so read-only costs nothing in the Installed tab; the Updates tab has no such guard (`UpdatesTab.tsx:74-86` sends `ops/update` for any row), so the guard is added there in the same commit as the first consumer of the per-project `unsupported` fact. `MainShell.tsx:143,147` counts every discovered project in "All Projects (N)" and `Project` (`src/protocol/domain.ts:27-32`) carries no support flag: that cannot change in this item and is recorded, not fixed.
(2) `ARCHITECTURE.md:553`, written by P5.5, says "All Projects shows an empty state until P5.9"; ledger N11 (`docs/plans/findings-ledger.md:114`, "All-projects update responses uncorrelated") is scheduled "P3.3, P5.9 … the all-projects slices that use it are P5.9, where this closes"; P5.10's row text names sash, context menu, title-bar toggles and Open full view, not All Projects; the plan row of P5.9 is "Feature all-projects". `Catalog.allProjectsUpdates` (`Catalog.ts:363-400`) streams one `project` chunk per project (`updates: []` plus `error` on failure), an `icons` chunk keyed by lower-cased id, and answers `sourcesUnavailable` on the result; `resourceKeys.allProjectsUpdates` (`domain.ts:232`) is a reserved key that is never in `keys` (ADR-009 item 1), so the stream follows the `updates:` keys and the committed `includePrerelease` (R8 shape, `src/webview/shared/store/updates.tsx:36-49`), not `installed:`. The bulk request exists: `ops/bulkUpdateAllProjects { projectUpdates: ProjectBulkUpdate[] }` (`messages.ts:46-50,160`). The slice-with-first-consumer rule (P3.6) and ADR-008's enumeration (`docs/adr/008-webview-architecture.md:25-27` names `allProjects`, no second all-projects slice) put the updates stream into `allProjects.tsx` beside the transitive stream the tree already has there.
(3) The fixture workspace is shared by every suite: `.vscode-test.mjs:12` and `package.json:316-317` open `src/test/e2e/fixtures/e2e-workspace`; `src/test/e2e/{v2-sidebar,install-flow,update-flow,file-watcher}.e2e.test.ts` take `findFiles('**/*.csproj', …, 1)[0]` (`v2-sidebar.e2e.test.ts:56-58`, `install-flow.e2e.test.ts:26-28`), whose order with two files is not guaranteed and whose assertions (`package remove Serilog` then "Newtonsoft.Json still referenced") need the chosen file to be `TestProject.csproj`; none of them is an item file (plan §2.1), so option a is a stop-and-ask on top of this one and option c (another workspace for the v2 UI suite) moves the `csprojPath` constant of three existing v2 UI tests and the `test:ui:v2` script. Option b leaves the row's ExTester test hollow for the feature whose core is the real slice's rule, which is what the per-feature ExTester test exists for (P3 review gap 2). The runtime-created project needs no change elsewhere because the host already does the rest: `src/extension.next.ts:309` watches `**/*.{csproj,fsproj,vbproj}` create with a `project` scope (1500 ms debounce), ADR-002's scope table (`docs/adr/002-query-coordinator.md:24`) maps `project{paths}` to the `projects` key, `extension.next.ts:244-246` refreshes the project list on a `project`-scoped invalidation and `:177` fires `projects/changed`, `SessionStore.ts:124-125` keeps `ALL_PROJECTS` with two projects, and `SessionStore.test.ts:295` pins the downgrade when the workspace shrinks to one, so a run that dies with All Projects persisted self-heals at the next activation (under option c it would not, and `main-installed` would fail on `installed-list` until `/tmp/nuiget-ui-v2` is wiped). It also proves more of P5.9's own path (watcher → `projects` → selector offers All Projects → fan-out) than a static folder would. `sdk-too-old` cannot be shown in VS Code on the runners: `src/core/project/context.ts:57-59` needs a parsed SDK with `supported === false`, and the runners have SDK 10 only; one workspace folder means `folders.length > 1` is false, so folder headings never render there either.
(4) `InstalledTab.test.tsx` is the test of a file the item edits (§2.1), the assertion encoded the P5.4-era absence that the P5.4 ruling itself scheduled P5.9 to end ("the all-projects transitive aggregate … P5.9"), interaction model §3 says the aggregate is "loaded lazily on expand", and the P5.5 ruling is the precedent for re-scoping a named test's assertion to the same intent. Option 2 drops an assertion; option 3 would give the same thing a second test id outside §8 for a test's sake.
`touchedBy` (`src/webview/shared/store/ops.tsx:104-125,131-139`): `OperationProgress` has the same `projectPaths`/`packageIds` shape, so the host's `ops/progress` marks the same cross product on every surface the moment it arrives; a finer local record changes nothing another surface sees and nothing for the common case (one package id across projects), and a finer protocol shape is a contract change this item may not make (D6). The deviation recorded in `src/webview/shared/STATUS.md:485-488` stays.

### P5.10 — stop-and-ask: commit split, Enter on a sidebar row, browse under All Projects, the two-phase transitive metadata (2026-10-16)

Brief: the P5.10 row's accumulated notes (sash, view state, re-show, context menu, Open full view, Enter re-read, N66,
