sidebar's All Projects); options: one commit or ordered green commits; three open readings (Enter, browse Enter under
All Projects, whose the two-phase ask is). Answer, verbatim:

`````text
CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF (checked first): "Only the tracker rows edited" is no longer true of the tree. `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` on `labs/2.0` @ a6c2b52 lists, besides `docs/plans/STATUS.md`, seven modified item files and one new one: `src/webview/shared/store/session.tsx` and `session.test.tsx` (the `visibilitychange` ask, with the test `asks session/get again when the document becomes visible, and a stale answer changes nothing`), `src/webview/sidebar-next/{SidebarView,InstalledSection,UpdatesSection,index}.tsx`, `sidebar.css` (the `Sash` between the sections, `SidebarLayout`/`ViewStateStore`/`readLayout`, controlled `expanded`/`share` props, `--nuiget-sidebar-share` through `cssVars`, the entry handing `acquireVsCodeApi()` to `SidebarView` as `viewState`) and untracked `src/webview/sidebar-next/SidebarLayout.test.tsx` (4 tests). That is most of note (i) and all of note (ii) already written; the ruling below takes it as commit (a)'s base and asks for one change to it. Two more facts the brief states as open are settled by the tree: `src/webview/shared/store/session.tsx:77-96` (working tree) already re-asks on `document.visibilitychange` and keeps `ui/focusSearch` as the focus request alone, which is what P3 review non-blocking 3 asked; and `src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts:189-228` (`computeInstalled`) emits only the `provisional` chunk when an evaluator exists and never a `metadata` chunk, while `src/webview/main/features/installed/InstalledProjectSection.tsx:41-53,123,130` reads `installed.metadata` for the description, the Vulnerable badge and the `@vulnerable` filter (answering "Vulnerability data is not available for this project yet." whenever the map is empty): in single-project mode that map is always empty today. Not `OWNER MUST DECIDE`: nothing here touches scope, release, publishing or a D-decision.

DECISION: Option B, as four green commits in this order, each with the §2.2 gates and the sidebar bytes pasted: (a) single-project parity in the webview (what is in the tree, with the layout written on `Sash.onChangeEnd` and the toggles rather than on every `onChange` step, plus Shift+F10/ContextMenu key/right-click → `ui/contextMenu` and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter → `ui/viewPackage` on the three sidebar lists); (b) the `installed` slice asks `transitive/metadata` with the rows of an answered `installed/get` (the interim ADR-009 d.1 describes); (c) the sidebar's All Projects: grouped Installed and Updates sections over the `allProjects` slice, and browse under All Projects through `ui/contextMenu`'s browse path (the host's QuickPick picker); (d) the host: `SidebarHost.ts:147-150` passes `sourcesUnavailable` through and says "No package source could be reached for this package", `src/host/pickers.test.ts`, the `src/host/**` ratchet key, the ExTester file, the docs. The three readings: (1) Enter on a sidebar Installed row stays uninstall; "View package details" is Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS, the Listbox's `onSecondaryActivate`) and the menu's item; uninstall stays on Enter, Delete, Cmd+Backspace and the row button. (2) Under All Projects, Enter, the `+` button and the menu of a browse row all send `ui/contextMenu` with `context: 'browse'`, `projectPath: ALL_PROJECTS` and `installedProjects`; the "Select a single project" sentence goes. (3) The two-phase `transitive/metadata` ask is this row's (commit b), in the shared `installed` slice, until P6.2 replaces it with the chunk.

WHY: Plan §2.1 (one item ≤ a session-day) and the P5.4/P5.9 precedent of ordered green commits inside one row fit a row that touches three directories and the ExTester suite; the order puts the webview-only work (already largely in the tree) first, so an interruption loses least, and the host change with its tests and the ExTester proof last, where `npm run package:vsix` is due anyway. Reading 1: interaction model §5 says "Enter activates the row (…sidebar: performs its primary action), Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) performs the secondary action, Delete (…) uninstalls where applicable, and Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key opens the actions menu"; the sidebar's Updates section (Enter = update) and browse list (Enter = install) already bind Enter to the row's action, 1.x binds Enter to `onAction` (`src/webview/sidebar/SidebarApp.tsx:1136-1140` per the P3 review), the Listbox's `onSecondaryActivate` (`src/webview/shared/primitives/Listbox.tsx:36,149-152`) is the model's unused slot, and the existing test `uninstall: Enter and Delete on the active row do the same as the button, and focus stays in the list when the row goes` (`SidebarView.test.tsx:185`) then stays byte-for-byte; a navigation Enter would have re-bound three lists against the model for no gain. Reading 2: §3 says "Install from browse opens a multi-select project picker (QuickPick in the sidebar…)"; under D6 the only request that reaches that picker is `ui/contextMenu` (`src/protocol/messages.ts:167`), whose host path `SidebarHost.showContextMenu` (`src/host/SidebarHost.ts:116-166`) already handles `isAllProjectsBrowse` with `pickContextMenuAction` → `pickProjectsForInstall` → `operations.install`/`bulkInstall`, reading `request.installedProjects` for the "(installed x)" annotations and the uninstall candidates; `ContextMenuRequest` (`messages.ts:84-94`) has every field needed (`installedProjects[].version` is required, so a project whose version is unknown is left out). The cost is one more QuickPick than 1.x (the actions menu before the picker; 1.x's `+` went to the picker directly, `ARCHITECTURE.md:929`): a recorded deviation, not a contract change. The same host path rejects `ALL_PROJECTS` for `installed`/`updates` (`SidebarHost.ts:118-121`), so a grouped row sends its own section's project path. Reading 3: ADR-009 d.1 as amended by P4.9a (`docs/adr/009-catalog.md:11`) reads "until P6.2 adds the provisional chunk to `installed/get`, the installed views ask it after `installed/get`"; the P4.9 ruling assigned that interim to "P5.4/P5.10" and P5.4 closed without it (deviation at `src/webview/main/STATUS.md:636`), so P5.10 is the last named carrier and the tree today contradicts the ADR for every single-project Installed list. The slice is the right owner (ADR-008: shared slices; `store/transitive.tsx:67-85` already does exactly this for its rows, and `installed.tsx:44-54` already keeps the per-project metadata map the P6.2 chunk will feed), the sidebar renders nothing of the map (`grep -rn "metadata" src/webview/sidebar-next --include='*.tsx'` excluding tests → 0; interaction model §1: compact rows, no icons or descriptions), and the sidebar's extra ask is cheap by construction: the lite lookups are cached per source (`src/core/catalog/feedClients.ts:85-100`). ### P6.2 — stop-and-ask: the evaluator, the provisional chunk, enrichment and the split (2026-10-15)
`````

Brief: plan §2.4 form, item P6.2, on `labs/2.0` @ `440b154` with nothing for P6.2 written; it asked for the approval
of the contract change and rulings on when an evaluation runs, the evaluator mapping, the place of enrichment, the
superseded evaluation, the webview slice, the split and the `nuget config paths` cadence. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: Approve P6.2 as a contract item, split into two tracker rows under the P4.9a/P4.9b precedent: P6.2a (the evaluator module, no frozen file, no wiring) and P6.2b (the contract behind the sentinel `P6.2b`, the Catalog, the webview slice, the root, the docs). The rulings, one option each: A1 with one correction: the `installed/get` chunk becomes `{ kind: 'provisional'; result: InstalledResult }` and REPLACES the `metadata` kind on that request (no product code emits it there; the other `metadata` chunks stay); ADR-009 d.1 and d.3 and one ADR-004 tier-2 paragraph amended; no A2 (ADR-007 needs no note: a chunk carries no generation already). B1: an evaluation runs for every supported project that has a context, cached by revision, which is the rule `Catalog.ts:209` already implements. C1, mirroring the inspector's `describe` (`inspector.ts:281-305`), implicit references kept and marked. D4, overriding the expectation recorded by the P4.9 ruling and the P5.10 ruling: the two-phase `transitive/metadata` ask of `installed.tsx` STAYS and enrichment does not move into `installed/get`; the chunk P6.2 adds is the provisional list alone. E1: the superseded evaluation stays as it is; rule 7 discards and re-asks. F1 restricted to data: the slice shows the provisional of the latest unanswered request as `result`, no new UI. G2. H1: no change to the `dotnet nuget config paths` cadence; N72 reassigned to P7.2. The Catalog's merge is corrected so that the evaluator's row wins. Nothing here is the owner's.

WHY: The brief describes the tree accurately (`Catalog.ts:110,152-227`, `handlers.ts:260-265`, `messages.ts:121`, `contracts.ts:316-321`, `commands.ts:136-159`, `installed.tsx:40-85`, `fakeDotnet.ts:167`, the five `evaluations` of `src/core/cli/__fixtures__/sdk-probes/10.0.401.json`), with one addition that decides D: nothing in product code emits the `metadata` chunk of `installed/get` (`grep` of `kind: 'metadata'` under `src/core/catalog`, `src/host` hits `allProjectsInstalled` and `search` only); three tests do (`handlers.test.ts:312-328`, `installed.test.tsx:135-158`, `InstalledTab.test.tsx:208`). D is settled by three recorded rules that cannot all hold for chunk-carried metadata: ADR-009 d.2 and ADR-002:18-19 (a cache hit and a late joiner receive the cached value and no chunk, and every second surface and every re-read of an unchanged project is a cache hit), ADR-007:19-21 (chunks precede the one terminal response, so metadata that lands after the authoritative result is undeliverable on that request), and the P4.9 ruling's own DO NOT (`docs/plans/STATUS.md:2316`: never delay the `installed/get` response on the network). The P4.9 ruling's WHY (3) chose the two-phase ask for exactly the first-paint reason; what it deferred to P6.2 was the provisional chunk, and ADR-009 d.1 as amended (`009-catalog.md:11`) says "until P6.2 adds the provisional chunk", so the sentence is rewritten under the sentinel rather than left stale. B is settled by ADR-004 tier 2 (`004-project-model.md:29-35`: runs off the render path, cached by revision, the UI upgrades when it lands) and by the fact that the inspector cannot tell what it does not see (imports beyond the nearest props file, `Directory.Build.targets`, the SDK's own items: `NETStandard.Library` appears only in the evaluation, fixture `multitfm-items-netstandard2.0`), so B2 would leave the "provisional" badge both surfaces already render (`InstalledSection.tsx:134`, `InstalledProjectSection.tsx:161`) on forever for a project it misjudged, and B3 contradicts `domain.ts:44`; the cost is one properties run plus one run per framework per project and revision (about 0.5 s each, P6.1), bounded by the coordinator, which caches the result (authoritative or provisional on failure) until the next invalidation of the key. The merge at `Catalog.ts:221` (`{ ...prior, ...pkg, … }`) keeps the inspector's `targetFrameworks`, `definedIn` and `isImplicit` when the evaluator's row has none, so an evaluation that proves a conditioned row is in every framework would still show the condition: the evaluator's row is complete and wins, and only `resolvedVersion` (the assets file, which the evaluator does not read) is kept from the inspection; `installed resolves before evaluator` (`Catalog.test.ts:181-204`) still holds under that expression (newtonsoft keeps `13.0.3` from the inspection, `Implicit.Sdk` comes from the evaluator with its own `isImplicit`). E1 is already enforced end to end: `useResource.ts:79-96` asks once more for an answer below the listed generation and ends as an error after a second one, `installed.test.tsx:124` (`R7`) and the harness's `rule 7: …` pin it, and E2 would rewrite ADR-009 d.3 ("never rejects") and a Catalog test the row does not name for one saved round trip in a race. The harness needs nothing: `fakeDotnet.ts:167` answers `msbuild` with no output and exit 0, which the evaluator treats as a failure that is not cached, so every scenario's terminal response stays the provisional with the same packages, plus one `provisional` stream envelope that `FakeWebview.ts:217,260` records and does not apply; the holds match `nuget config paths` (`fakeDotnet.ts:97`) and msbuild spawns only after that walk resolved, so none of `recomputation.seen` (`scenarios.test.ts:119,125,142`), `count(configPaths)` (`:270`) and `walk.seen` (`:455,692`) moves. H1 follows from the same: "cache by revision" in the plan row is the evaluator's cache (ADR-004 tier 2), keyed by the revision that `ProjectContextProvider.get` computes (`context.ts:37-60`), so the walk stays per computation and the six scenarios the brief names stay untouched; N72 is a `FeedContexts`/root matter that P6.2 does not touch. G2 follows plan §2.1 (P6.2 spans `src/core/project`, `src/core/catalog`, `src/host` tests, `src/webview/shared/store`, `src/protocol`, two ADRs and the root) and the P4.9 precedent; the seam leaves P6.2a's tree green with `tsc` 0 (the module is exported and unused, which is not a stub: `CatalogDeps.evaluator?` has been optional and unfilled since P2.8 by that ruling's design).

3. `src/core/project/evaluator.ts`: `export interface EvaluatorDeps { runner: DotnetRunner; stopDirs?: readonly string[]; logger?: Logger }` and `export class MsBuildProjectEvaluator implements ProjectEvaluator`. Imports: `../contracts` (types), `../cli` (`msbuildGetArgs`, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`; `feeds/search.ts` sets the precedent for `project → cli`), `../logging` (`redact`), `../util/paths` (`normalizeProjectPath`), `./central` (`findCentralPropsPath`, `parseBooleanProperty`), `./rows`. No `child_process`, no `Thenable`, no Node ≥ 20 API.
   - `evaluate(context, signal?)`: key `normalizeProjectPath(context.projectPath)`; cache `Map<string, { revision: string; result: Promise<InstalledResult> }>` with one entry per project: a hit with `entry.revision === context.revision` returns `entry.result` (the promise, so two callers of one revision share one evaluation); otherwise store the new promise and delete the entry when that promise rejects (successes only; a failure is never cached, the coordinator's cached provisional bounds the retries).
   - Properties run: `runner.run(msbuildGetArgs(projectPath, [], ['TargetFramework', 'TargetFrameworks', 'ManagePackageVersionsCentrally', 'CentralPackageVersionOverrideEnabled']), { cwd: context.projectDir, timeoutMs: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, signal })`, exactly the four properties of the P6.1 probe (never one property alone: `-getProperty` with a single name prints the bare value, not JSON). DO NOT:
- Do not move enrichment into `computeInstalled` or `Catalog.installed()`, and do not hold the `installed/get` response for a feed answer; the P4.9/P5.10 expectation is overruled here, by name.
- Do not keep the `metadata` chunk kind on `installed/get` as a dead member, and do not touch the `metadata` chunks of `allProjects/installed` and `search/query`.
- Do not evaluate only when the inspection "looks uncertain", and do not relabel a provisional result `authoritative`.
- Do not request a single property with `-getProperty`, parse stdout with a bare `JSON.parse`, or build argv by hand; `msbuildGetArgs` only, through `DotnetRunner.run` (ADR-003).
- Do not cache a rejected evaluation, a timeout or a cancellation, and do not add an LRU keyed by a composite string; one entry per project, keyed by its revision.
- Do not give the evaluator an `AssetsReader`; `resolvedVersion` stays the inspection's.
- Do not keep `{ ...prior, ...pkg }` in the merge; the evaluated row is complete.
- Do not make `upgrade` reject on a stale generation or retry inside the handler; rule 7 handles the race.
- Do not change `useResource`, `ProjectContextProvider`, `FeedContexts.register` or the config-paths cadence; the harness counts stay.
- Do not teach `fakeDotnet` to answer `msbuild` in this item (P6.4), and do not add a harness scenario that depends on it.
- Do not add `cachedFidelity` consumers, a `generation` on the chunk, or per-project pairs to `OperationProgress` (P5 review 1: only if P6.4 needs them).
- Do not create the sentinel in P6.2a, before the tracker rows exist in P6.2b, or with content other than `P6.2b`; do not commit while it exists; do not start P6.2b before P6.2a's CI run is green.
- Do not raise a bundle ceiling, an e2e timeout or the host ratchet to get a gate green.
`````

### P6.4 — stop-and-ask: the preview request, the dialog's choices, the sidebar, the harness and the split (2026-10-15)

Brief: plan §2.4 form, item P6.4, on `labs/2.0` @ `232d54c` with nothing for P6.4 written; it asked how the CPM
preview reaches the webviews (a contract change), which choices the dialog offers, central uninstall, bulk updates,
the sidebar, the unresolved tooltip and the provisional upgrade, the harness and the split. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: A1 + B1 + C1 + D2 + E-host (a better E the brief did not list: the sidebar's central update goes through the host's actions menu, and the host confirms with a VS Code modal before submitting; no `Dialog` enters the sidebar bundle) + F-tooltip (a `versionTitle` on `Row`, nothing else is missing) + G1-opt-in (the fake answers `msbuild` from the files only when the scenario asks; the existing scenario keeps its title, a new scenario carries the gate's title) + H2 as three sub-rows: P6.4a (contract + host, sentinel `P6.4a`), P6.4b (harness fake + gate scenario), P6.4c (webviews + interaction model). CONTRACT CHANGE: one request, `cpm/preview`, and the move of `CpmImpactPreview` from `src/core/contracts.ts` to `src/protocol/domain.ts` (exact text under CONTRACT CHANGE). Nothing here is the owner's.

WHY: The brief is right about the tree on every path it names, and misses one live defect that decides E: since P6.3b the sidebar's QuickPick path runs a central edit with no preview at all (`src/host/SidebarHost.ts:204,214` submit `operations.update`, `:191,198,216` submit `operations.install` with a version; `DefaultProjectMutator.canMutate` admits a CPM install/update on SDK 10 with a version, `src/core/project/mutator.ts:59-71`), which violates interaction model §5 row 73 and ADR-004 tier 3 ("CPM mutations show an affected-projects preview", `docs/adr/004-project-model.md:41-43`); the preview therefore has to exist host-side anyway, and §1 and §3 of the interaction model already put choices in QuickPicks/modals on the sidebar and dialogs in the main panel, so routing the sidebar's central update through `ui/contextMenu` costs no bytes against the 11 427 of headroom (N63, P5 review 5). A2 fails because the sidebar never holds the fan-out and the main panel only in All Projects; A3 would tell the user after the fact what ADR-004 says must be shown before; so the preview reaches the main panel through a request, which is a contract change under D6 (`scripts/hooks/guard.mjs:36` freezes `src/core/contracts.ts`, `src/protocol/**`, `docs/adr/**`; `docs/ux/**` is not frozen). B3 is out: no SDK command writes a `VersionOverride`, the extension edits no project file (ADR-003; `mutator.ts:4` "never writes a file: the edit itself is the CLI's") and the mutator refuses override rows until a probe row exists (N74, `mutator.ts:53-55`), so the dialog offers one action and §5 row 73 is amended, not silently deviated from. C1 because a single uninstall on a CPM project removes the project's own reference only and never the central entry (ADR-004 tier 3 `:44`, plan gate `never deletes central entry on single uninstall`, probe row `remove` in `src/core/cli/__fixtures__/sdk-probes/10.0.401.json`: project diff only); there is nothing to preview, and the mutator admits every remove (`mutator.ts:44-47`), so `whyNotRemovable`'s central branch (`src/webview/shared/installed/rules.ts:38-40`) goes and §4 row 57 / §5 row 73 say so. D2 because a bulk of central rows would need one preview per row inside `UpdateAllDialog`; it is a separate finding, not this item. The gate scenario's second act is feasible without a core change: the execution context is rebuilt per computation and its revision covers `Directory.Packages.props` (`src/core/project/revision.ts:11-12,46`), so the evaluator cache (`src/core/project/evaluator.ts:56`) misses after the fake's props edit. Two `affectedProjects` lists exist and the tests must not confuse them: the mutator's preview includes the asking project (`mutator.ts:102-105`), the workflow strips it from the outcome (`src/core/ops/PackageWorkflows.ts:234-242`).
`````

`````text
DECISION: Option 1, bounded: one more `gh run rerun 38792875987 --failed` (a third attempt of `E2E 2.0 (stable)` alone), no code, test or CI-configuration change, and no commit before the outcome. Green → P6.4a is landed; the run is recorded as the third sighting of N65 in P6.4b's commit. Red a third time → mark P6.4a `blocked`, commit the tracker and STATUS edits as a docs-only commit, push, and stop with the RUN.md §8 report. Not `OWNER MUST DECIDE`: nothing here is scope, release or publishing.

WHY: The brief is accurate, and the protocol requires none of the four options by itself. RUN.md §5 step 3 ("after two red runs mark the item `blocked`") counts fix-forward cycles of a code failure (push → red → fix in a new commit → push → red); here there is one run, two attempts and nothing to fix forward. The gotcha row "A red CI run is not always a code failure" (`.github/copilot-instructions.md:173`) is the environmental exception to that counter and routes a second identical failure on one SHA to this stop-and-ask, which ledger N65 (`docs/plans/findings-ledger.md:416`) and the P3 phase review (`docs/plans/STATUS.md:531`) anticipated; the ruling, not §5.3, decides. Same VS Code build `07b4ff1883f9` (1.142.0) and same runner image `ubuntu-24.04 20261012.334.1` passed that job on the previous SHA 70 minutes earlier and passed this SHA's 1.x `E2E (stable)` concurrently (job 116621662078); `UI 2.0` on this SHA passed 32 tests of the 2.0 build on the same image, on VS Code 1.140.0 (ExTester's pin, not 1.142.0). ### P7.1 — stop-and-ask: the legacy key list, the shared cache prefix, migration and the Breaking wording (2026-10-16)
`````

Brief: plan §2.4 form, item P7.1, on `labs/2.0` @ `93bfd17` with nothing written; the plan's "9 legacy `nuget.*` keys"
is contradicted by the tree (8), and 1.x and 2.0 share the `nuiget.cache.` prefix. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: A2 + B1 + C1 + no migration (D) + two new `**Breaking:**` lines (E). Sweep nine literal keys (seven workspaceState `nuget.*`, two globalState: `nuget.splitPosition`, `nuiget.sdkVersionCache`) plus every workspaceState key under `nuiget.cache.` that `nuiget.cache.__index__` does not list, from a new `src/host/legacyState.ts` called once per activation before `TieredCache` and `DefaultSessionStore` are constructed; the orphan discriminator is a pure helper exported from `src/core/cache` so the index key and prefix stay private to `TieredCache.ts`. The brief is wrong on two points, corrected below. Plan count: 8 literal `nuget.*` keys, not 9.

WHY: The brief's reading of the tree is wrong in two places. (1) 2.0 does persist layout in mementos: `src/host/handlers.ts:241-255` reads and writes `nuiget.layout.splitPosition` (globalState) and `nuiget.layout.sidebarSectionSplit` (workspaceState) for `layout/get`/`layout/set` (ADR-001:29 "the host only persists layout preferences (`layout/*`)"); `vscode.setState` holds only the webview-side state. These two keys are live 2.0 state and never swept. (2) The count: `git grep -ohE "['\"]nuget\.[A-Za-z]+['\"]" main -- src ':!src/**/*.test.*'` and the same on `labs/2.0` both list exactly eight memento keys (`includePrerelease`, `recentSearches`, `restoreEnabled`, `restoreEnabledMigrated`, `selectedProject`, `selectedSource`, `sidebarSectionSplit`, `splitPosition`); the plan's "9" is supported by neither tree (`nuiget.noRestore` is a configuration setting, `nuiget.layout.*` is 2.0's own); read "9 legacy keys + sdkVersionCache" as 8 + 1 and record it as a finding. Seven of the eight live in workspaceState; `nuget.splitPosition` is globalState (`src/webview/NuGetPanel.ts:1266,1277`), as is `nuiget.sdkVersionCache` (`src/extension.ts:31`). A3's premise is false: `TieredCache.clear()` (`src/core/cache/TieredCache.ts:146-153`) iterates `this.persisted.keys()`, `loadPersistedIndex` (`:239-268`) reads only the keys named in `nuiget.cache.__index__`, and `evictPersistedIfNeeded` budgets only tracked entries; nothing in `TieredCache` ever calls the store's `keys()`, so a 1.x `WorkspaceCache` entry (`src/services/WorkspaceCache.ts:18`, up to 500 entries including search results, version lists and READMEs, `src/services/NuGetPackageService.ts:1069,2272,2426`) is never read, evicted or cleared by 2.0 for the life of the workspace. That is the orphan state the item is named for; the index is the safe discriminator (a 2.0 entry whose index flush never landed is equally unreadable, so deleting it loses nothing). ADR-000:21-22 ("replaced without migration shims … Users re-select project/source once") and the item's own "removed migration" settle D: migrate nothing. A marker key (C2) is itself a shim and breaks a developer who alternates `watch` and `watch:v2` on one workspace; the every-activation sweep is nine `get`s and one `keys()` walk, and writes only for keys that exist. `KeyValueStore` (`src/core/contracts.ts:31-35`) has no `keys()` and is frozen (D6), so the sweep takes the VS Code mementos in host code (`src/host/**` may import `vscode`, §3 fences); `Memento.keys()` is in the pinned `@types/vscode` and already used at `src/services/WorkspaceCache.ts:220`, and `createMockExtensionContext` implements it (`src/test/__mocks__/vscode.ts:356,366`). Tracker row P7.1 (from P2.10) asks that `LEGACY_SDK_CACHE_KEY` (`src/extension.next.ts:31,76-78`) be folded in so the key is swept in one place.

DO:
1. `src/core/cache/TieredCache.ts`: add and export a pure function `orphanedStoreKeys(store: { get<T>(key: string): T | undefined; keys(): readonly string[] }, storePrefix = DEFAULT_STORE_PREFIX): string[]` returning every key of `store.keys()` that starts with `storePrefix`, is not `storePrefix + INDEX_KEY`, and is not `storePrefix + k` for a string `k` in the index array (no index, or a non-array index → every prefixed key). Re-export it from `src/core/cache/index.ts`. No `vscode` import, no change to `KeyValueStore`.

A second case with no index at all returns every prefixed key.

Rewrite `src/host/STATUS.md` and `src/core/cache/STATUS.md` (§2.5), paste this ruling under Advisor decisions in `src/host/STATUS.md`, list the rewritten test of step 6 by old and new title, and close the P7.1 row with the 8-vs-9 note.

DO NOT:

Do not write `'nuiget.cache.'` or `'__index__'` anywhere outside `src/core/cache/TieredCache.ts`; a copy in the host is the "deletes live 2.0 state" failure the moment either constant changes.
`````

### P7.2 — stop-and-ask: scope, the ceiling reset, the perf numbers, the evaluator cancellation, N72 and the N65 diagnostic (2026-10-16)

Brief: plan §2.4 form, item P7.2, on `labs/2.0` @ `54885d4` with nothing written. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: A1 with the assignment below (P7.2 becomes an umbrella row with P7.2a "CI, ceilings, perf baseline" and P7.2b "evaluator cancellation"; P7.2c and P7.2d exist only if a measurement opens them); B1 (ceilings reset to Math.ceil(measured × 1.1) at the P7.2a commit, bytes and SHA in the comment, as the P3.6 ruling dictated); C1 for the dotnet-side numbers (a new informational `perf` job running `scripts/perf-baseline.mjs` over the e2e fixture and a tracked multi-TFM copy of it) combined with C3 for search (the `[P5.6] cold search` line plus a new `[P7.2] warm search` line from the `ui-v2` job's log), the doc written once from the first CI run with its run id; D2 (the evaluation runs are bound to no caller's signal; a caller whose signal is already aborted at the call starts nothing; the per-run 60 s timeout bounds the work), not D1; E: decide now — N37 and N65 get one signature-gated in-step retry in both e2e jobs (no verbose logging, no `continue-on-error`), N72 is accepted with its measured unit cost and the fix shape recorded, not fixed; F: `RESTORE_TIMEOUT_MS` changes only by a mechanical rule from the measured cold multi-TFM restore. The `found` chunk on `search/query` (⚑) is not done in P7.2 and opens a row only if the cold search exceeds its target on two consecutive runs. Nothing here is the owner's; no `OWNER MUST DECIDE`.

WHY: The brief matches the tree with one correction that matters for where `--analyze` goes: the `e2e-v2` job builds explicitly (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:311`, `node esbuild.mjs --v2 --production`), and only `ui-v2` goes through `vscode:prepublish` (`:357-358`), so the 2.0 table can be enforced on `e2e-v2`'s build step without touching `npm run package`; the `build` job (`:420`) builds 1.x the same way and keeps the flag through the P8.1 flip, when the 1.x table dies with it. B1 is not the "silent raise" the gotcha row forbids: that row and the reset to measured × 1.1 come from the same P3.6 ruling (`docs/plans/STATUS.md:1973,1978`), the row governs a *build that crosses* a ceiling, and this reset is recorded in the comment, the tracker and the ledger (N63), with P8.2 re-measuring and ratcheting again after `bench:save`; the P1.x numbers (`esbuild.mjs:28-36`) stay untouched. On D: `installed()` goes through `coordinator.query` on one key (`src/core/catalog/Catalog.ts:154`) and `evaluate(` has one call site (`Catalog.ts:211`), so two concurrent callers of one revision never exist; the defect of the P6 review (2) is sequential — `invalidate` aborts the running computation's signal synchronously (`src/core/queries/QueryCoordinator.ts:203`, `:251` on dispose), the recompute reaches `evaluate` only after `computeInstalled` has re-awaited the inspection and the config walk (`Catalog.ts:187-200`), and finds the cached promise of `evaluator.ts:56-58` bound to the dead signal. A per-entry controller aborted "when every joined signal has aborted" is already aborted by then and restarts 1+N runs; no caller signal lets the next generation (manual refresh = workspace scope, same revision; A→B→A) join the in-flight promise and get `authoritative` with no restart, which is the option that loses the least work; the cost is that an evaluation of a changed revision runs to its end (≈ 0.5 s per run, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` 60 s bound, `evaluator.ts:110`) and is dropped by `cache.set` of the new revision (`:62`) and by the coordinator's "an old completion cannot repopulate" (ADR-002 invariant 3). ADR-004 tier 2 ("off the render path, cached by revision") and the frozen `ProjectEvaluator.evaluate(context, signal?)` signature are unchanged. N72 stays open-to-accepted rather than fixed: the only fix shape (`contexts.get` joining the pending chain `forDirectory` stored in `chains`, `src/core/catalog/feedContexts.ts:89-96`, or an in-flight dedupe in `configFilesFor`, `src/core/project/context.ts:77`) joins a walk across an invalidation and can hand the new revision a chain read before a `nuget.config` edit, and the harness pins the walk counts by hold (`src/test/harness/scenarios.test.ts:117-142,208,245,270,283,320,528,765`); the cost is one extra `dotnet nuget config paths` (the perf script measures it) running concurrently at mount, Low. The retry is not `continue-on-error` (P3.6 DO NOT): a run in which Mocha printed any `N passing`/`N failing` line is never retried, the first attempt's output stays in the artifact (the diagnostic half of the ledger's "verbose logging or a job-level retry"), and the retry is annotated. The combined `-getProperty`/`-getItem` run is timed in the perf script but adopted nowhere until a probe row exists (P6.2 ruling, DO NOT "build argv by hand"); the probe fixture `src/core/cli/__fixtures__/sdk-probes/10.0.401.json` is tracked, not frozen, and `--check` in CI compares `evaluations`, so a new row and the regenerated fixture must land in one commit — that is P7.2c's, opened only if the measurement pays.

DO:
`````

### P7.2c — ⚑ ruling: the combined first run, its probe rows and its guard (2026-10-16)

Brief: plan §2.4 form, item P7.2c, on `labs/2.0` @ `87e9d18`, nothing written. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: Option 1 with its guard corrected (call it 1'): the first run is one combined `msbuildGetArgs(projectPath, ITEMS, PROPERTIES)` run with no global property; its items are the result only when the properties' `TargetFrameworks` is empty (a project with `TargetFramework` alone, or neither); when `TargetFrameworks` is set, at all, the items of that run are discarded and one item run per framework with `-p:TargetFramework=<tfm>` follows, as today. Probe rows `cpm-combined` and `multitfm-combined`, both without a global property; the `multitfm-combined-<tfm>` rows named in the tracker row (my own wording in step 11 of the P7.2 ruling) are dropped: they would probe a run the product never makes, because the first run cannot carry a framework it does not know yet. Two commits with a green `SDK probe` job between them: the rows and the regenerated fixture first, the evaluator second. Not option 2 (its `TargetFramework ==` guard is a tautology once `TargetFrameworks` is empty and a weaker test of the cross-targeting case than reading `TargetFrameworks` itself; the single-entry `TargetFrameworks` case needs no new input, because 1' treats it as cross-targeting and runs exactly today's argv for it). Not option 3: the 400 ms rule of the P7.2 ruling already decided that the change pays. Nothing here is the owner's; no `OWNER MUST DECIDE`.

WHY: The brief matches the tree (`src/core/project/evaluator.ts:87-96` properties run then one item run per framework; `scripts/probe-sdk.mjs:305-312` builds the probe argv by hand in its own form; `src/core/cli/__fixtures__/sdk-probes/10.0.401.json` has the five `evaluations` ids; `--check` compares `evaluations` by id, argv, exitCode and output through `projection`, `probe-sdk.mjs:160-170`), with four scope facts it did not list: `src/core/cli/sdk.test.ts:107-113` hard-codes the five evaluation ids and goes red the moment a row is added; `src/test/harness/fakeDotnet.ts:197-214` answers `Properties` alone to any call carrying `-getProperty:`, so a combined call would read `Items` as `{}` and the one `evaluate: true` scenario would end authoritative with zero packages; `src/test/harness/scenarios.test.ts:419` asserts `count(msbuild(C1)) >= 2` for a single-framework project, which becomes 1; and every ad-hoc fake in `evaluator.test.ts` branches on `-getProperty:` the same way (seven tests, named below). Option 1's "≥ 2 entries" guard is wrong by the tree's own evidence: the outer evaluation of a cross-targeting project has `TargetFramework` empty (`multitfm-properties`: `"TargetFramework": ""`, `"TargetFrameworks": "net8.0;netstandard2.0"`), and the per-framework rows show that the conditional `System.Text.Json` and the SDK-implicit `NETStandard.Library` exist only in the `netstandard2.0` run (`multitfm-items-netstandard2.0` vs `multitfm-items-net8.0`; `src/core/cli/STATUS.md:63-66`), so a `<TargetFrameworks>net8.0</TargetFrameworks>` project evaluated without the global property would list the outer build's items; "`TargetFrameworks` non-empty" is the condition MSBuild itself uses for the outer build, and under it 1' runs today's argv unchanged. The evidence that the single run is equivalent for a single-framework project is the regenerated `cpm-combined` row: its `Properties` must equal `cpm-properties`' and its `Items` must equal `cpm-items-net8.0`' (the `cpm` input sets `<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>`, so the global property `-property:TargetFramework=net8.0` of the item row only restates it); that equality becomes a tracked test, and if the regenerated fixture fails it the evaluator does not change. ADR-004 tier 2 (`docs/adr/004-project-model.md:29-33`) spells the run shape ("a properties run …, then one run per target framework"), so the evaluator change without an amendment would be a contract/ADR mismatch (plan §2.3 universal trigger); D6 allows an advisor-approved contract-change item, and this ruling approves one sentence there behind the sentinel. The P6.2 ruling's DO NOT ("build argv by hand") holds: the product uses `msbuildGetArgs(projectPath, ITEMS, PROPERTIES)` (`src/core/cli/commands.ts:136-159`: `-getItem:` joined with `,`, `-getProperty:` with `;`), the probe keeps its own form, and the evaluator test asserts argv through `msbuildGetArgs`, as `evaluator.test.ts:101-105` does today. `ProjectEvaluator.evaluate(context, signal?)` in `src/core/contracts.ts` is untouched, as is P7.2b's no-caller-signal rule (`evaluator.ts:58-77`).
`````

### P7.3 — stop-and-ask: the red Windows job of commit 1 (N54, N80) (2026-10-16)

Brief: plan §2.4 form, step 7 of the P7.3 ruling, on `labs/2.0` @ `8c3ca04` (CI run 38829853849 red on `Test (windows-latest)` only). Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: Option 1. One commit (commit 2 of the P7.3 ruling, brought forward, cited as the fix-forward of RUN.md §5 step 3 for run 38829853849): the `try { … }`/`catch { … }` pair in `decryptPassword` becomes the single entropy statement, the unit test gains the two `not.toContain` assertions of step 8, a new ledger finding (next free id; N80 at this tree) records the parse defect and is closed in the same commit, N54 is closed citing test B of the red run and test A of the new run, CHANGELOG gets one `### Fixed` headline, and the tracker row becomes `done`. Not Option 2 (an intermediate commit of a form the next commit deletes, which spends CI on nothing test B has not already shown and risks the second red run), not Option 3 (a defect in a file the ruling put on the item's list, `NuGetConfigReader.ts`, is fix-forward under RUN.md §5 step 3, not the owner's).

WHY: The brief is right about the tree: `src/core/sources/NuGetConfigReader.ts:161-169` builds the script as seven array elements joined with `'; '`, and `:165` (`try { … }`) and `:166` (`catch { … }`) are separate elements, so the script `powershell.exe` receives reads `… ; try { … }; catch { … }; …`; test B (`NuGetConfigReader.test.ts:191-196`) keeps its `try { … } catch { … }` inside one element, which is the only material difference between the two scripts, and test B passed in the same job. PowerShell's grammar admits only new-lines between a `try` block and its `catch` clause (`catch-clause: new-lines_opt catch …`); a `;` ends the `try` statement, which then has no `catch` or `finally`, a parse error that fails the whole script before `Add-Type` runs (not run here: this machine has no `powershell.exe`, and `decryptPassword` discards stderr, so the log cannot show the message). The one other way to the observed `undefined` is a timeout kill (`powershell.ts:87`, `exitCode -1`), and the log rules it out by arithmetic: test A took 4152 ms in total including `dotnet nuget add source`, below `DECRYPT_TIMEOUT_MS` = 5 000 (`:147`) on its own. The `$null` branch was therefore never a fallback but the cause of the failure, and the entropy fact the ruling's commit 2 waited for is now evidence (job 116745869544: `Unprotect($bytes, UTF8('NuGet'), CurrentUser)` printed the password with exit 0, the `$null` form hit the `catch` marker), so step 8's precondition is met in substance and dropping the branch is also the smallest change that removes the parse error. Without a `try`, a failed `Unprotect` leaves `$plain` unset, `GetString($plain)` throws, nothing is written, and `:171` answers `undefined` on the empty stdout whatever the exit code, so the contract of `decryptPassword` ("never rejects, `undefined` when it cannot decrypt") and the test `answers undefined when PowerShell fails or prints nothing` (`:206`) are untouched. The defect dates from `402acbd` (P2.6; `git log -S"catch { \$plain"`), the unit test `dpapi: decrypts through runPowerShellEncoded …` (`:135`) checks script text only, and `DefaultCredentialProvider.ts:79` is the one product caller, so 2.0 has never decrypted an encrypted `nuget.config` password on Windows while `DotnetSourceProvider.ts:105` writes them; that is a product defect worth its own ledger id, and this red run is the first of RUN.md §5 step 3's two. The ubuntu job of the same run (116745869536) is green with `NuGetConfigReader.test.ts (13 tests | 2 skipped)` and `Tests 3414 passed | 2 skipped (3416)`, which fixes the expected counts below; the first ruling's `3414 | 1 | (3415)` was off by one.
`````

### P7.fix-2 — follow-up ruling: the two entry tests that pin the start requests (2026-10-16)

Brief: P7.fix-2 DO 3 implemented; `src/webview/main/index.test.tsx:36` and `src/webview/sidebar-next/index.test.tsx:35` (not named by the P7.6 ruling) fail because `perf/mark` is a start request. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
Follow-up ruling on P7.fix-2, DO 3 (the two entry tests that pin the start requests):

DECISION: Option 1. Both entry tests are rewritten by title (this answer names them, so plan §2.1 allows it): the expected start set gains `perf/mark`, the titles gain "and marks webviewReady", and ARCHITECTURE.md:623 names the mark. The `status === 'ready' && result !== undefined` reading is right; the ruling's `'ok'` was my error (the union at `src/webview/shared/store/useResource.ts:10` is `idle | loading | ready | error`).

WHY: The two tests exist to pin the start set (`src/webview/main/index.test.tsx:36`, `src/webview/sidebar-next/index.test.tsx:35`), and `perf/mark` is now a real start request by the P7.6 ruling's DO 3, so the pinned set must say so; filtering it out (option 3) would hide the one request the fix adds from the test that documents the start set. Sending the mark after the first `session/get` answer (option 2) would make "webview ready" mean "host answered", couple a diagnostic to a data request, and change nothing about the pinned set anyway. The gotcha "Re-requesting `projects/list` on invalidation" concerns the count of `projects/list` on invalidation, which the mark does not touch (harness 22 passed confirms); the e2e suites assert behaviour, not the request set.

DO:
`````

### P7.fix-1/P7.fix-3 — stop-and-ask: the second red Windows job, run 38873696417 (N84) (2026-10-16)

Brief: plan §2.4 form, the case pre-registered by DO 11 of the P7.fix-1 ruling, on `labs/2.0` @ `12219e7` (CI run 38873696417 red on `Test (windows-latest)` only), with the P7.6 bookkeeping prepared and uncommitted. Answer, verbatim:

`````text
DECISION: Option 2 as a new tracker row `P7.fix-3`, test-only: test A warms PowerShell once with its own 60 s budget (a DPAPI round trip of a dummy value) before the product-budget `decryptPassword(stored)`, asserts the warm-up succeeded, and logs the cold-start and decrypt durations with `console.warn`; `decryptPassword`, `powershell.ts`, the 10 000 ms default and `DefaultCredentialProvider` stay as P7.fix-1 left them. P7.fix-1 stays `done` (its fix is proven by the now-visible `Error: DPAPI decryption timed out after 10000 ms`; the "different cause" DO 11 pre-registered is confirmed and named below), the P7.6 acceptance at `68d034d` stands, and the session continues to P7.6 and the P7 boundary once the P7.fix-3 run is green.    ```ts
   /**
    * The first `powershell.exe` of a Windows job is a cold start (CLR, System.Security, the DPAPI user key) and took longer
    * than the product budget next to a concurrent real-SDK restore (CI run 38873696417, N84). The product treats a cold
    * timeout as transient and asks again (N83); test A therefore measures the product path on a PowerShell that has
    * started once, and logs the cold start so every Windows job adds a measurement.
    */
   async function warmPowerShell(): Promise<number> {
       const started = Date.now();
       const result = await runPowerShellEncoded([
           'Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Security',
           "$bytes = [System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData]::Protect([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes('warm'), $null, [System.Security.Cryptography.DataProtectionScope]::CurrentUser)",
           '[Console]::Out.Write([System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData]::Unprotect($bytes, $null, [System.Security.Cryptography.DataProtectionScope]::CurrentUser).Length)',
       ].join('; '), { timeoutMs: 60_000 });
       expect(result).toMatchObject({ exitCode: 0, stdout: '4' });
       return Date.now() - started;
   }
   ```
`````
